stories.title: Weather changes across UP:Strong winds and rain lash 6 cities; monsoon likely within 3–4 days
stories.summary: The wait for the monsoon in UP is increasing. The monsoon has stalled after reaching the state's border. This has led to an increase in heat. People are suffering due to the humidity. Since Tuesday morning, most cities have experienced strong sunlight. The heat is palpable. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the monsoon's entry into UP may take more than a week. For now, the heat will continue to show its intensity for a week. Today, there is an alert for rain in 16 cities and a heatwave in 38 cities. IMD states that usually, the monsoon enters UP by June 20. However, this time, after reaching the UP-Bihar border, the monsoon is unable to advance further. For the past 15 days, it has been stalled near Maharajganj. There are chances of it advancing today or tomorrow and reaching UP by June 28-29. In the last 24 hours, Prayagraj (43.3 °C) was the hottest city in the country. Gorakhpur, Siddharthnagar, Basti, Mau, Ghazipur, and Ballia received rain. In Basti, trees and poles were uprooted due to a storm and rain. A tree fell on a car. A unipole falling on the road caused heavy traffic jams. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- Currently, no weather system is active in UP, due to which heatwave conditions prevail in Eastern UP. The temperature will rise for the next one week. The Southwest Monsoon has advanced over South and Central India. It is likely to advance further in the next 48 hours. After this, a gradual increase in weather activities can also be seen in North India. How will the weather be in UP for the next 5 days? Know

stories.title: 10 coaching centres sealed in Indore:Administration takes action a day after Lucknow tragedy
stories.summary: Ten coaching centres and buildings were sealed in Indore on Tuesday, a day after 15 people were killed in the Lucknow coaching centre fire tragedy. One of the deceased in the Lucknow accident was software engineer Jayneel Chakraborty (26), a resident of Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh. A joint team of Indore administration, municipal corporation, and fire department raided several coaching institutes. Serious safety flaws were found at Catalyzer Coaching Center located in Geeta Bhawan. The building's emergency exit was closed. Nucleum Coaching Institute, Ramanujan Coaching Institute, Aayam Coaching Institute, Makhan Wala Hotel, and Ikrath Coaching Institute were also sealed. Inspection from Veda Business Park to Apollo Arcade The joint team inspected coaching centres as well as major commercial complexes in the city. During this, the fire safety arrangements of several commercial buildings in Veda Business Park, Apollo Avenue, Apollo Arcade, and Bhanwarkuan area were checked. The investigation found that fire-fighting systems in many buildings were faulty. They were not installed in accordance to the rules. In some places, regular maintenance of the fire safety system was not done. The administration issued notices to the building operators. Emergency exits found closed in multi-storey buildings During the inspection, emergency exits were found closed in several multi-storey buildings. In case of fire or other disaster, it is mandatory for such routes to be open and safe. Closed emergency gates can affect the safe evacuation of people. Inspection of coaching centres and libraries Under the leadership of SDM Ghanshyam Dhanger, the raids, dubbed 'operation coaching centre', was conducted. The raids are expected to continue. SDM Dhanger said action is also being taken against buildings where other commercial activities are being run along with coaching institutes and where adequate fire safety arrangements are not in place. Some restaurants, museums and other offices were also sealed. Officials said the safety of students is the top priority. They clarified that strict action will continue against negligent institutes and buildings. Relief will be granted upon implementing fire safety arrangements SDM Dhanger said the administration has clarified that the purpose of sealing is not to permanently close institutions, but to ensure compliance with safety regulations. Building operators will have to give an affidavit assuring that they will install necessary fire safety equipment and security arrangements within 15 to 20 days. Sealed buildings will reopen after submitting documents After the prescribed procedure is completed and safety standards are complied with, the concerned buildings and institutions be allowed to reopen.

stories.title: UP serial rapist killed in encounter:Abducted and raped 6 girls; had escaped from Punjab jail
stories.summary: In Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, police shot dead a 65-year-old serial rape accused during an encounter. The accused, Satpal alias Sattu, a resident of Punjab, had spent a total of 16 years in prison—11 years in Muzaffarnagar and 5 years in Ludhiana jail. He had escaped from Ludhiana jail in February 2026 and had been hiding in Muzaffarnagar and nearby districts since then. According to police, the encounter took place on Monday night around 11:30 pm when Sattu was apprehended after an exchange of fire. One bullet hit his leg and another struck above his waist. He was initially admitted to hospital, but his condition deteriorated on Tuesday and he died around 1 pm. Doctors said the cause of death was excessive blood loss. SSP Sanjay Verma stated that Satpal alias Sattu used to kidnap girls and rape them. He added that since February, the accused had allegedly targeted six victims. In one such case on June 19, he allegedly kidnapped a minor girl after luring her with a job offer and later raped her. Following the complaint, a case of kidnapping of a minor was registered at Civil Lines police station. Ten special police teams were formed, and a reward of ₹25,000 was announced for information leading to his arrest. Police teams from four states were also involved in the search operation. During the investigation, CCTV footage from around 1,000 cameras was examined and surveillance inputs helped trace his movements. Police said he had taken the victim to Punjab after kidnapping her, where she was kept captive and assaulted before being moved again via a bus route through Yamunanagar. This picture is from Monday night at 11:30 PM. Police arrested Sattu in the encounter. He was hit by two bullets. One above the waist and the other on the leg.Police claimed that Sattu had first fired at the police vehicle. One constable was injured in this. While another constable was injured during the encounter. SP explained how Sattu's encounter took place SP City Amrit Jain informed, “On Monday night at 11:25 PM, a joint team of police and SOG was conducting checking on Bamanhedi-Rudki Road. During this time, a suspicious car with a Punjab number plate was spotted. When police signaled it to stop, the driver started fleeing with the car. The police team chased the car and surrounded it.” “Upon this, the accused abandoned the car and started firing rapidly at the police team. This resulted in 2 constables getting injured. In the police's retaliatory firing, Sattu was hit by 2 bullets. He became seriously injured. He was admitted to the hospital,” he added. From the spot, police recovered a .32 bore pistol, cartridges, fake Aadhaar card, mobile phone, the car used in the crime, and gold earrings of the kidnapped girl. Sattu linked to Chhota Rajan gang, had over 24 cases in 3 states Police have identified the deceased accused Satpal alias Sattu as a member of the Chhota Rajan gang. According to officials, he was a resident of Ramdarbar Sector-32 in Chandigarh and his father’s name was Munnu Ram. Police said Sattu had been an active shooter and member of the notorious Chhota Rajan criminal network. Officials further stated that more than 24 cases are registered against him across three states, including serious charges such as murder, robbery, rape, and kidnapping.

stories.title: VIDEO | Alcohol, non-veg party on boat in Ganga:Five arrested in Varanasi, face up to 5 years in jail
stories.summary: Five boatmen have been arrested in Varanasi after a video allegedly showed them consuming beer, alcohol, and non-vegetarian food while on a boat in the Ganga River. The video, which was widely shared on social media, reportedly shows the men cooking chicken, drinking beer and liquor, and serving non-vegetarian food during the gathering. Case registered under BNS provisions Following the video's circulation, the Dashashwamedh police outpost in-charge filed a complaint, leading to a case under Sections 196 and 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which relate to promoting enmity and acts allegedly hurting religious sentiments. Police arrested all five accused and seized the boat. They are expected to be produced before a court, and the offences may carry penalties of up to five years’ imprisonment, depending on the charges proved. See 2 pictures of the non-vegetarian party on the boat Police identify the accused The arrested individuals have been identified as Deepak Kumar, Ajay Sahni, Arun Kumar Sahni, Anurag Nishad, and Rahul Sahni. According to police, they are residents of Varanasi and nearby Ramnagar. Authorities said the video appears to have been recorded during the winter season, though its exact date is still being verified. Previous similar controversy Police also referred to an earlier incident in March, when an iftar gathering held on a boat in the Ganga drew controversy after videos circulated online showing non-vegetarian food being served. That incident led to a separate police case and multiple arrests after complaints from local groups.

stories.title: 16-yr-old kills brother, sister-in-law and nephew:Accused says family made him quit studies, treated him like a dog
stories.summary: “I was very good at studies. I studied up to 5th grade in a CBSE school. I came first in class every time. After this, my father made me drop out of school. I somehow studied up to 10th grade by working as a laborer. I failed 10th grade due to lack of time. After this, my family members started taunting me even more. My family members collectively made me drop out of school. They used to insult me daily at home. Many days I didn't even get food. I had to search for a place to sleep in my own house.” This is what the 16-year-old accused boy, who murdered his elder brother, sister-in-law, and nephew in Bansgaon, Gorakhpur, said. After committing the crime around 3 am on Monday morning, he was sitting in a room on the second floor of the house. He had no remorse for committing the murder. He confessed during police interrogation, "I wanted to torture and kill my father in the same way." The police asked, "What will you do now?" Then he said, "I didn't get food at home, but in jail, my stomach will be full both times." Then the police asked, “What will you do after being released from jail?” He said, “Whatever fate has in store, that will happen.” Saying this, the accused started crying loudly. He kept repeating that he wanted to study, but he was not allowed to study. He had dreamt of becoming an officer by taking the UPSC exam. Accused says, “Dog died after eating home food.” The incident occurred on Monday at 3 AM in Balua village, under Bansgaon police station, 50 km from the district headquarters. The murdered were identified as Amit Gupta (35), his wife Ranjana (32), and son Reyansh. The police interrogated the accused for about two hours. During this, the accused stated that his family members always treated him like a dog. “Three years ago, my sister-in-law left food outside my room, just like for a dog. I took the food and threw it outside. A village dog ate that food. Shortly after, it died. Since then, I felt that there was a plan to kill me at home too. I worked hard in my father's carpentry shop, but I didn't get a single penny,” the accused said. “I used to call my elder sister and ask for money to recharge my mobile. I wore torn and old clothes; new clothes never came home for me. Many times, mutton was prepared from Tarkulha, but it was not served to me. The family members would eat it among themselves,” he said. Man demands death penalty for his son After losing their son, daughter-in-law, and grandson, father Harilal and mother Anita Devi are inconsolable. Harilal, weeping, demanded Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to ensure his son is sentenced to death at any cost. “My younger son killed his elder brother, sister-in-law, and three-year-old grandson while they were sleeping, using a gym rod and a cleaver at night,” the father said. “My younger son was asking for money, which led to disputes many times. If he had to kill someone, he should have killed me; what wrong did my elder son do to him? I have cancer, and my wife is undergoing treatment for her heart condition,” he said. "In such a situation, I was unable to provide money. He didn't understand this at all. He was only concerned about himself. He had no concern for his family," he added. Meanwhile, mother Anita Devi was unable to stay conscious after the remembering the incident. Anita said, "May God never give such a child to anyone; he destroyed the entire family." Amit had adopted his sister's daughter People in Balua village are shocked by the actions of this 'Kalyugi' son (a son of the Kali Yuga, implying evil/unrighteous). Ramsajeevan, from the village, said Amit was very friendly. He was married 15 years ago. He did not have children of his own, following which he adopted his younger sister's child. Her age is now 9 years. Meanwhile, three years ago, after receiving medical treatment, his wife gave birth to a son. The little child used to play outside the house; everyone in the locality loved the child. The accused killed Amit, his wife, and son, but did not kill the adopted niece. The young girl said that her uncle first killed her father, then cut off her mother's and baby's heads. She immediately ran away screaming, and told everything to her grandmother. “I kept saying repeatedly - don't kill my baby, in one swift stroke, he cut off his and my mother's heads,” the girl said. Head crushed with a rod, then throats slit with a cleaver The bodies of Amit Gupta, his wife Ranjana, and their son Reyansh were sent for post-mortem at BRD Medical College. The post-mortem report stated that severe injuries were present in the head and neck which caused the deaths. Amit's head was attacked seven to eight times with a rod. Ranjana's head was hit twice, and Reyansh's throat was slit. According to the police, the accused was most angry with his father and elder brother. Therefore, he repeatedly hit his elder brother's head with a gym rod. He wanted to torture him to death. The younger son had fought with his father, a compromise was reached at the police station. Father Harilal has filed a complaint against his accused younger son. Harilal said that he had a carpenter's shop a short distance from home in the town. The elder son, Amit, used to do paint and polish work outside. Two years ago, he started sitting at the shop. This made the younger son unhappy. Two months ago, there was also a dispute between the father and the younger son. The younger son was asking his father for ₹5 lakh to start work. After this, a compromise was reached at the police station. The younger son used to come home drunk and caused disputes almost daily. Psychiatrists says such activity is called psychopathic. Psychiatrist Dr. Amit Kumar Shahi said, “This type of activity is called psychopathic behavior. It can be due to many reasons. Sometimes social ups and downs mentally disturb people, making them feel inferior. People related to them often misinterpret things.”

stories.title: Kanpur seals over 30 coaching centres after fire:KDA cracks down on institutes violating building and fire safety regulations
stories.summary: Following the deadly fire at a coaching centre in Lucknow, the Kanpur Development Authority (KDA) has launched a large-scale inspection drive in Kakadeo, one of Uttar Pradesh’s biggest coaching hubs. More than 30 coaching institutes have been sealed for allegedly violating building and fire safety norms. Many were reportedly operating commercial activities from residential buildings without complying with mandatory regulations. Inspection teams check every building Acting on the state government's directions, KDA formed four special teams to inspect coaching centres across the area. Officials have been examining buildings one by one since Tuesday morning. While 16 institutes were sealed by Monday night, the number rose to over 30 by Tuesday afternoon. Focus on student safety KDA Secretary Abhay Pandey said the action was taken to prevent incidents similar to the Lucknow tragedy, as thousands of students study in Kakadeo every year. He said authorities are inspecting coaching centres and other commercial establishments to ensure they meet safety standards. Fire safety and basements under scrutiny The inspection is focusing on buildings lacking adequate fire safety measures, emergency exits, or those operating from basements without approved plans. Authorities warned that any institution found violating construction, usage, or fire safety regulations would face sealing and legal action under relevant laws. Similar drive conducted earlier KDA officials said this is not the first such campaign. Around six months ago, a special drive led to the sealing of more than 100 basements and coaching institutes for similar violations. The current campaign has been expanded, with teams instructed to inspect every street and building in the area to ensure compliance with safety norms.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at coaching centre in Agra:Students rush onto street from second floor; another incident reported after Lucknow
stories.summary: Within 24 hours of the deadly fire in Lucknow that claimed 15 lives, another fire scare unfolded at a coaching centre in Agra on Tuesday. Smoke reportedly billowed from the basement following a suspected short circuit, prompting the swift evacuation of more than 100 students attending classes. According to eyewitnesses, smoke suddenly began rising from the basement, after which the coaching management immediately ordered all classrooms to be evacuated. Students were escorted out in an orderly manner, while local residents rushed to the spot. The incident triggered brief panic in the area, though no injuries were reported. Police and fire officials inspect premises After receiving information about the fire, police and fire brigade officials reached Akash Coaching Centre and inspected the premises. Authorities found that the institute had adequate fire safety arrangements in place. However, during an inspection of GS Coaching Centre nearby, officials identified serious safety deficiencies. They noted that the entry and exit passages were extremely narrow and several fire extinguishers were found to be empty. The administration issued a stern warning, directing the coaching management to immediately improve safety measures or vacate the premises. Both the coaching operator and the building owner were summoned by the police. See 2 pictures... Student: ‘Teachers told us to leave the classroom immediately’ Student Poonam said she was attending a botany class when staff members and teachers suddenly entered and instructed everyone to leave the classroom without delay. “We weren’t given any information at first. Our teachers asked us to move out quickly and led us outside in lines. We initially thought the classes had been dismissed or that something important had come up,” she said. “Later, we were informed that a transformer in the ground-level area had caught fire. That was all we knew.” ‘About 50 students were in our classroom’ Another student, Aryan Pandit, said around 50 students were present in his classroom when the evacuation began. “Our teachers came in and told us there was a fire. We immediately exited through the fire escape and saw many students already outside,” he said. “There wasn’t much panic because we couldn’t see smoke inside the classroom. We only knew that a fire had broken out somewhere in the building. The teachers ensured that everyone was evacuated quickly.”

stories.title: ‘Save us’ calls haunt families after Lucknow fire:Father faints on seeing son’s body, sister breaks down in tears
stories.summary: The bodies of all 15 victims who died in the Lucknow coaching centre fire underwent post-mortem examinations over nearly seven hours on Monday night. After the process was completed, the bodies were handed over to their families. Scenes outside the mortuary were heartbreaking. One father reportedly fainted after seeing his son’s body, while grieving relatives broke down in tears. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to 6 family members. They said that after being trapped in the fire, the children called home, informed them about the fire, and pleaded for help to save their lives. But, by the time we arrived, it was too late. Many victims made last calls for help According to family members, several victims managed to call their loved ones after becoming trapped inside the burning building. They informed them about the fire and pleaded for help, but rescue could not reach them in time. See 5 pictures- Read the pain of the families of 5 people who lost their lives in the accident Abdul Rehman supported his family Abdul Rehman, an IT technician from Lucknow, had recently secured a job after a long wait. Friends said he had started working at a young age to support his family, as his father was paralysed. His family said he called home after getting trapped in the fire. His parents were too distressed to visit the mortuary immediately. Sukhmani Singh tried to escape Sukhmani Singh’s father said his son called around 2:30 PM, saying, “Papa, there is a fire. Please save us.” Relatives said Sukhmani had left for work happily that morning and had planned to spend the evening with his family before the tragedy struck. Aditya’s sister missed his final call Aditya Srivastava, a 3D character artist from Sitapur, also lost his life in the blaze. His sister said he had called her while trapped inside the building, but she was unable to answer. According to the family, several people took shelter inside a bathroom hoping to survive the fire, while another relative escaped by jumping from a window. Mother collapses after seeing daughter’s body The family of Anamika, who worked as an animation artist in Lucknow, travelled from Kolkata to collect her body. Her mother collapsed in grief after seeing her daughter, while relatives recalled that Anamika had spoken to them normally before leaving for work on the day of the incident. Marriage plans ended in tragedy Twenty-one-year-old Nilesh, another victim of the fire, was reportedly planning to marry his colleague Anamika. According to family members, both families had begun discussing the match and were preparing to meet soon. The plans were cut short by the devastating fire, leaving both families in mourning.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft probe report submitted:SIT recommends FIR, five-year audit trust restructuring measures suggested
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) on Tuesday submitted its investigation report to the Uttar Pradesh government in the alleged Ram Mandir donation theft case. According to media reports, the SIT report recommends registering an FIR in the matter, reconstituting the temple trust, and appointing a senior official as the temple's Chief Executive Officer (CEO). The SIT has also sought additional time for a more detailed investigation, and has claimed that the submitted report is an initial one. The 150-page preliminary report was submitted to Sanjay Prasad, Additional Chief Secretary of the Home Department. The SIT stated that the report includes details of the questioning of 150 individuals. According to sources, the SIT has recommended an audit of the temple's donations over the past five years. It has also proposed measures to prevent irregularities in the handling of donations and raised questions about the role of certain office-bearers of the temple trust. Sources further said that the state government will forward the report to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, which will decide whether any members of the trust should be retained or removed. In the Ram Temple theft case, investigators have recovered ₹2 crore based on information provided by five accused—Lavkush, Avneesh, Anukalp, Karune, and Ramshankar alias Tinnu. Gold was also recovered from the residence of Tinnu, who is considered a close associate of Champat Rai, a key member of the Ram Mandir trust. According to preliminary estimates, the alleged theft could exceed ₹200 crore.

stories.title: Lucknow building to be razed:48 coaching centres sealed in UP; Akhilesh Yadav seeks ₹1 crore aid for victims' families
stories.summary: A total of 15 people have died in the fire at a two-storey building in Lucknow. On Tuesday morning at 11 am, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) and a forensic team reached the site to investigate the tragedy. The team inspected the building, and the SIT, which includes IPS officer Praveen Kumar and IAS officer Amrit Abhijat, collected evidence and left with bags containing material from the scene. The post-mortem examinations lasted for seven hours before the bodies were handed over to their families. The mother of 30-year-old Anamika from West Bengal collapsed after seeing her daughter's body at the post-mortem house. The investigation has revealed that the building where the fire broke out was illegal. A demolition order had been issued in 2016 but was later cancelled. Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar said the building owner has been served a notice and asked to respond within 15 days. He added that the building will be demolished. The building belongs to Virendra Shukla, owner of Rameshwaram Institute of Technology and Management College. Police have registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and arrested four accused, including Virendra. stories.title: Ayodhya DM assumes charge of Ram Mandir administration:Three major changes introduced, donation counting process overhauled
stories.summary: The investigation into the alleged misappropriation of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir has reached its final stages, with the Special Investigation Team (SIT) completing its preliminary probe and preparing its report under the leadership of SIT chief Vijay Vishwas Pant. Given the religious significance of the case and its impact on millions of devotees, the report will first be submitted to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). Only after receiving approval is legal action expected to begin. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is reportedly monitoring developments in the matter. Ayodhya DM oversees Ram Mandir operations Amid the ongoing investigation, Ayodhya District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi, who serves as an ex-officio member of the Ram Mandir Trust, has assumed oversight of the temple’s day-to-day administration. According to the report, trust members who previously handled operational decisions are no longer actively involved in routine management Three major changes introduced in donation management Following the launch of the investigation, temple authorities have significantly tightened procedures related to donation handling and staff supervision. 1. Cash counting shifted to floor-based process Previously, volunteers counted donation box cash while seated at tables and chairs. The process has now been shifted to floor mats and carpets, with strict frisking of staff before and after counting sessions. Video recording of cash removal from donation boxes has also been made mandatory. 2. Staff replaced and surveillance strengthened Only 40 trusted volunteers have been assigned to count donations. Earlier personnel, along with two bank employees involved in the process, have reportedly been replaced. Six new CCTV cameras have been installed, and digital video storage capacity is being expanded. 3. Trustees’ operational powers frozen Trust General Secretary Champat Rai, trustee Dr. Anil Mishra, and invited member Gopal Rao are no longer participating in routine administrative decisions and are reportedly barred from making fresh operational decisions related to temple management. Administrative supervision is currently being carried out under the District Magistrate’s oversight. Key trust officials keeping low profile According to sources cited in the report, Champat Rai, who earlier resided at Karsevakpuram, has been staying within the Ram Mandir complex since the donation controversy surfaced and has not been leaving the premises. Dr. Anil Mishra reportedly visits the temple daily before returning to his residence in Lakshmanpuri Colony, while Gopal Rao, who lives adjacent to the temple complex, continues to visit regularly. Employees from whose residences cash was allegedly recovered are reportedly being kept in a basement inside the temple premises, where police and officials are conducting questioning. SIT report divided into 3 sections The Special Investigation Team has structured its findings into three major components: Criminal investigation The probe examines whether negligence or misconduct by employees or trustees resulted in the disappearance of cash donations, jewellery, or other temple assets. Financial audit Investigators have reviewed donations received so far, banking transactions, tender procedures, and land purchase and sale records associated with the temple trust. Reform recommendations The SIT is expected to recommend changes to trust regulations, improved security mechanisms, and enhanced accountability measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. Trustees may be removed from responsibilities According to sources, senior trust functionaries, including Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao, are unlikely to receive a clean chit in the investigation. While they may not face direct allegations of theft, they could be held accountable for negligence and administrative lapses. The report further claims that discussions between the government and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) have resulted in a broad consensus to gradually remove the three individuals from trust responsibilities in the coming period. FIRs and arrests likely after final report With public scrutiny and political attention focused on the alleged donation irregularities, authorities are expected to adopt a zero-tolerance approach. The preliminary report has already been completed, while the final report is expected within 15 days. Once submitted, the Ram Mandir Trust may file formal complaints leading to FIRs against those found responsible. Several temple employees, including Anukalp Mishra, Somesh Anand, Ramshankar Yadav (Tinnu), D.K. Tiwari, Manish Yadav, Lavkush Mishra, Rajesh Pathak, and contractual workers Ratnesh Chaturvedi and Gagandeep Singh, are reportedly under investigation over allegations related to recovered cash or irregularities in donation counting. Any arrests or legal proceedings will depend on the conclusions of the final investigation.

stories.title: Automatic gate malfunction in Lucknow coaching claims 15 lives:Only one staircase for entry and exit; residential building was converted to commercial
stories.summary: The Lucknow coaching centre fire incident claimed 15 lives. Most of the deceased were students who came to learn gaming and animation. At the time of the incident, all students were in class after lunch. Initial investigation has revealed that the building had only one exit route from the outside. The main gate of the coaching centre was also automatic. It opened and closed through thumb impression. A student said that due to the fire, the thumb impression-based gate got locked, trapping most of the students inside. There was no alternative emergency exit. Within a few minutes of the fire breaking out, the entire building was filled with smoke. At the time of the incident, around 30 students and staff members were inside. While 8–10 students managed to escape using internet, DTH cables and pipes, 3–4 students jumped down from the second floor. Around 5–6 injured students are still admitted in KGMU. The building belongs to the owner of Rameshwaram Engineering College The building where the fire broke out is constructed on land owned by Virendra Shukla. Virendra Shukla is the owner of Rameshwaram Engineering College. The college is known as Rameshwaram Institute of Technology and Management (RITM), established in 2008. The college is affiliated with Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU) and is approved by AICTE. Investigation has revealed that the building map was passed in the name of Dhirendra and Surendra Shukla. Initially it was a residential building, but in 2014 it was approved for commercial use. An online animation and gaming coaching centre was running in the building. Due to summer vacations, a large number of students had enrolled here. After the incident, the administration has started an investigation into the role of the then officials and engineers. A list of 16 people has been prepared against whom action will be taken. Biometric system got locked due to fire An injured student’s friend, Yash, said that there was only one entry-exit point to go up and down. A biometric system was installed there. During the fire, the biometric system stopped working, due to which the children inside could not open the gate in time. The investigation has revealed that there was only one entry and exit route in the building. There was also only one staircase for movement. There was no alternative emergency exit. Even the door leading to the roof was locked. This is why many students could not escape in time amid smoke and chaos. Fire broke out due to explosion in AC compressor Initial investigation suggests that the fire may have started after a blast in the split AC compressor installed in the building. The spark from it spread to nearby items and furniture, causing the fire to engulf the entire building within minutes. Officials also believe that a short circuit could be a possible reason. However, the exact cause will be known only after the forensic and technical investigation reports are received. At present, agencies are examining all possible causes. Children tried to save themselves by locking themselves in the bathroom After the fire broke out, smoke first spread on the lower floors and then rapidly moved upwards. People on the upper floors panicked due to the sudden incident. Many tried to rush outside. Some locked themselves in rooms and bathrooms. There was chaos and screaming inside. Condition worsened due to suffocation According to fire officials, after the fire broke out, thick smoke filled the building quickly. Due to this, students and others inside could not find their way out. Some students hid in bathrooms while others moved into store rooms to save themselves. However, due to dense smoke and heat, many became unconscious. When the rescue team entered, several people were found unconscious. Fire officials said that the staircase leading to the roof was locked, preventing students from reaching a safe exit. To escape the smoke, they kept trying to hide in different parts of the building. First fire brigade vehicle reached 8 minutes after receiving information According to the fire department, the information about the fire was received at the control room at 2:27 pm. The first fire brigade vehicle reached the spot within just 8 minutes, followed by additional fire tenders, hydraulic platforms, and SDRF and NDRF teams for rescue operations. Rescue teams entered by breaking the rear wall Considering the severity of the fire, fire services, SDRF, and NDRF teams broke the rear wall of the building to enter inside. After that, rescue operations were carried out amid smoke and debris. According to officials, an attempt was made to enter by breaking a nearly 9-inch thick rear wall of the building. However, due to its strength, it took time to break, delaying access to unconscious students and others. Preliminary information suggests that plastic and aluminium sheet partitions and interior work were used in the office. This caused the fire to spread rapidly. A pet shop located on the ground floor had pedigree, packaging material, and other plastic products, which further accelerated the fire. According to rescue personnel, three types of chemicals used for pet treatment and care were also stored in the pet shop and clinic. After the fire, the smoke became highly toxic, affecting students on the upper floors first. Many became unconscious due to suffocation and toxic fumes within minutes. 15 cats were also inside, survived amidst the smoke Firefighters said that around 15 cats were present on the premises. Despite being exposed to smoke for a long time, they survived due to their biological resilience, whereas humans were affected much faster by the toxic fumes. A police officer rescued a cat from the fire and carried it out in his arms. Why did the fire spread so rapidly?

stories.title: Why UP BJP took 6 months to form new team?:Two key reasons emerge as party plays OBC card against PDA; Yogi kept distance
stories.summary: BJP's state executive's new team was announced 6 months late. More than 50% new faces have been given responsibility, sidelining those who had been in their positions for a long time. Now, preparations are underway to promote big faces. BJP wants to reduce the 'pressure politics' of its coalition partners. This is why, despite the alliance with RLD in the west, Gurjar and Jat leaders were given preference. The same was done with Rajbhar and Maurya faces in Purvanchal. 25 office bearers are from the OBC category alone. Along with the announcement of the list, there is also a discussion in political circles that CM Yogi did not intervene much. First, let's understand how this list got delayed by 6 months According to party sources, there was a long tug-of-war between the central and state leadership in finalizing the list. Two reasons emerged for this- Conflict over Yuva Morcha - There was a tough competition between Nikhil Mani Tiwari, Harshvardhan Singh, and Rohit Mishra for the post of Yuva Morcha's regional president. Different powerful leaders within the party were lobbying for all three. There was also constant opposition among them. This is why it took time to reach a consensus on one name. Finally, Rohit Mishra's name was finalized. Rohit was previously serving as the Vice President in Yuva Morcha. Kashi Region's Complication - The name of Kashi's regional president is decided directly with the consent of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This is why it took a long time for this post to be finalized. Yogi maintained distance, Dharmpal-Pankaj Chaudhary's preferences dominated The biggest political signal was that CM Yogi did not interfere at all in the functioning and appointments of the organization. Most of the names in the entire list were included based on the preferences of General Secretary (Organization) Dharmpal Singh and State President Pankaj Chaudhary. The coordination between him and Dharmpal Singh can be seen as 'Delhi-Lucknow tuning'. The only leader in this team considered close to the Chief Minister is Kameshwar Singh, who has been made the state vice-president. However, experts say that Kameshwar has been the state president of the Kisan Morcha. This is why his selection is considered appropriate. Veterans removed, some to be promoted Many big wickets have also fallen in this reshuffle. Veteran leaders like Vice Presidents Triyambak Tripathi, Santosh Singh, and Vijay Bahadur Pathak have been removed from the state team. This is giving many big signals in the state's politics. It is being discussed that even though Amar Pal Maurya and Govind Shukla, who were removed from the post of state general secretary, may not have got a place in the UP team. But, they can be given a big responsibility in the central team of BJP National President Nitin Naveen. Therefore, taking these powerful general secretaries from UP to the center shows that they are being 'promoted' instead of being 'angered'. This is an exercise to maintain the upper caste and Maurya (OBC) equation at the national level. 'Perform or Go Out' message The changes are like a major surgery for the organization, which was accused of sluggishness after the Lok Sabha election results. Bringing in more than 50% new faces by removing long-serving leaders proves that the party has given a 'perform or go out' message. This is to infuse new enthusiasm among grassroots workers before the 2027 assembly elections. BJP's 'OBC Card' against PDA The party has paid special attention to social engineering this time. In this 54-member team, 27 office bearers have been made from the OBC category. Here too, balance has been achieved by giving representation not to a single caste, but to all major castes falling under OBC. Political analysts believe that a similar trend was seen during the expansion of the Yogi cabinet. Now, backward classes have been given importance in the organization as well. This message could prove to be a game-changer for BJP in the 2027 elections. Political equations balanced for 2027 Countering SP's 'PDA' Narrative - BJP has included 21 Savarna (upper caste), 25 OBC, 7 Dalit, and 1 ST. An attempt has been made to completely break the casteist narrative. At the same time, efforts have been made to address the dissatisfaction of the Savarnas. Reduced Dependence on Alliance Partners - BJP has an alliance with RLD in the West, and with SBSP and Apna Dal in Purvanchal. Despite this, prominent positions have been given to Gurjar, Rajbhar, Maurya, and Chauhan leaders in the organization. This shows that BJP does not want its independent vote bank to weaken. 16 Faces included from Purvanchal In Pankaj Chaudhary's team, 16 office-bearers are from Purvanchal (Gorakhpur and Kashi regions). From Gorakhpur are State Vice President Dharmendra Rai, State Vice President Kameshwar Singh, and Ramesh Singh. Meanwhile, there are 9 office-bearers from the West. There are 10 office-bearers from Awadh region, 8 from Braj, and 3 from Kanpur region. Out of the 6 state presidents of frontal organizations, 4 frontal organizations' state presidents are from Purvanchal. Rohit Mishra, the State President of Yuva Morcha (Youth Front), is also from Pratapgarh, Purvanchal. Devendra Singh, the State President of Kisan Morcha (Farmers' Front), is from Azamgarh. Saroj Kushwah, the State President of Mahila Morcha (Women's Front), is from Ghazipur, and Vidya Bhushan Gond, the State President of ST Morcha (ST Front), is also from Varanasi.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan Singh receives death threat:Youth writes, 'Will shoot him openly and bring the entire system down'
stories.summary: Former BJP MP Brijbhushan Sharan Singh received a death threat on Thursday evening after a threatening post was shared on Facebook by a person identified as Pandit Shankar Dutt Shukla. The post, uploaded around 6:30 pm, warned of targeting the former MP and made violent remarks against the system. In the post, Shukla claimed that he always carries out what he says and wrote that the entire system would be set on fire. He also stated that Brijbhushan Sharan Singh would be openly targeted. Following a complaint, Gonda Police launched an investigation into the matter. Brijbhushan Sharan Singh is a former BJP MP from the Kaiserganj constituency. The person who issued the threat identified himself as a BJP leader The youth who threatened on Facebook has identified himself as a youth leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party. His Facebook profile shows his residence as Ayodhya. This post was made at 6:30 PM. Kaiserganj MP representative Sanjeev Singh has filed a complaint regarding this. Sanjeev Singh stated that he received a Facebook post. In it, Pandit Shankar Dutt Shukla has threatened to 'target' Brijbhushan Sharan Singh. A complaint has been filed with the police demanding strict action against the person who issued the threat. City Kotwal Bindeshwari Mani Tripathi stated that no complaint letter has been received by them yet. Strict action will be taken once the letter is received. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Shankar Dutt Shukla, who allegedly issued the threat. Read the conversation… What did you write to Brij Bhushan Singh? I wrote what I felt was right to Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. Why shouldn't I? During the Ram Temple movement, my grandfather supported him. He also stood alongside Atalji. I am going through a difficult situation and believed that my issue would be resolved through Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. However, he did not answer a single one of my calls. When one of his aides answered, he said, "Netaji is not available." Is that the way to respond to someone? My grandfather's name is Ram Kuber Shukla. I am a resident of Gilauli village in the Itiyathok police station area. Why did you write on Facebook that "we will shoot him"? I was angry, so I posted it on Facebook. I had been trying to contact him for nearly two months, hoping my issue would be resolved. It was related to a land dispute. Yes, I wrote the post myself. I am facing some personal difficulties, which is why I kept calling him. I have no personal enmity with Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, nor do I actually want to shoot him. Did someone ask you to post it on Facebook, or did you write it yourself? It is a personal matter. Either he should shoot me, or I will shoot him—that is what I wrote in anger. When ordinary people are not heard, what are they supposed to do? Please convey my message to him. If I cannot meet him, then let him shoot me instead. Please make sure Brij Bhushan Singh is informed about the situation. Anyway, I made a mistake. I admit it and apologise. Threats received before It was June 14. Brijbhushan's son and BJP MLA Prateek Bhushan was on a tour of the area. At 2:22 PM, he received a call on his mobile from an unknown number. As soon as he received the call, the young man on the other end said - Are you Prateek Bhushan? Listen, we will kill you and your father, Brijbhushan Singh. Arrangements for this have been made. If you can save yourself, then save yourself. The call lasted for about 35 seconds. After giving the threat, the young man hung up the phone. After this, Prateek Bhushan informed Gonda SP Vineet Jaiswal about the matter. Upon receiving the information, the SP issued instructions for action. The investigation by Nagar Kotwali police revealed that the young man who made the threat is mentally challenged. He was identified as Sandeep Sharma, a resident of Alwar district in Rajasthan. He is undergoing treatment at SMS Hospital Medical College in Jaipur. He has previously obtained mobile numbers of several public representatives and threatened them. Several cases have been registered against him in various places. Threats received before It was June 14. Brijbhushan's son and BJP MLA Prateek Bhushan was on a tour of the area. At 2:22 PM, he received a call on his mobile from an unknown number. As soon as he received the call, the young man on the other end said - Are you Prateek Bhushan? Listen, we will kill you and your father, Brijbhushan Singh. Arrangements for this have been made. If you can save yourself, then save yourself. The call lasted for about 35 seconds. After giving the threat, the young man hung up the phone. After this, Prateek Bhushan informed Gonda SP Vineet Jaiswal about the matter. stories.title: FIR filed in Ram Mandir donation theft case:Tinnu Yadav among 8 named; top trust officials left out
stories.summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on Thursday lodged an FIR in connection with the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir. Eight people have been named as accused in the case. As many as 3 people have been arrested as well. The complaint was filed by trust member Krishna Mohan based on the preliminary findings of the Special Investigation Team (SIT). The SIT was constituted on 13 June to probe the allegations and submitted its report to the Uttar Pradesh government on 23 June. Those named in the FIR include Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, driver to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai, along with Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra, Avinash Shukla, Manish Yadav, Ramashankar Mishra, Subhash Chandra Srivastava and Karunesh Pandey. Champat Rai's name does not figure in the FIR. Earlier in the day, AAP MP Sanjay Singh submitted 11 documents related to the alleged land scam linked to the temple to the SIT. He met SIT chairman Vijay Vishwas Pant at his Lucknow office and handed over the documents. Speaking to reporters afterwards, Singh claimed that evidence of both financial irregularities and theft of offerings had already surfaced. He questioned why no arrests had been made and why an FIR had not been registered earlier despite the findings. “One revelation after another is coming to light. Cash recoveries have already been made and evidence relating to alleged theft from Mandir donations has surfaced. Yet no one has gone to jail so far. Why has nobody been arrested? Why has no FIR been registered? This is extremely surprising,” said Sanjay Singh. Kejriwal alleges SIT Is focusing on junior staff AAP chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also reacted to the case, saying he was saddened by the allegations of theft of offerings at the Ram Temple and would visit Ayodhya on Friday to offer prayers. Meanwhile, reports circulating on social media claiming that Trust General Secretary Champat Rai had resigned were dismissed by temple construction in-charge Gopal Rao. He said no resignation had been submitted and urged people not to believe rumours, adding that the SIT investigation was ongoing and the truth would emerge once its report was released. VHP national general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra also rejected the resignation claims. Separately, Kejriwal alleged that the SIT was focusing on lower-level employees while avoiding action against those responsible for the alleged irregularities.

stories.title: From cricketing glory to spiritual bliss:Akash Deep's marriage in Kashi steals spotlight; wedding stage resembled cricket field
stories.summary: On Wednesday, Indian fast bowler Akash Deep began a new chapter of his life in Kashi, exchanging wedding vows with Akshita in a grand ceremony attended by family members, friends and prominent guests. The wedding stage was designed to resemble a cricket ground, reflecting the groom's sporting journey. As he stood beside his bride, Akash Deep appeared visibly delighted, celebrating the occasion with the same enthusiasm he displays on the cricket field. A celebratory moment on stage In a light-hearted moment, Akash Deep raised his bride's hand and flashed a victory sign, symbolising celebration and happiness. As Akshita approached him for the traditional exchange of garlands, he smiled warmly, bowed his head and accepted the garland. The couple then exchanged garlands and greeted guests with folded hands. The ceremony was met with loud applause from those present, while family members showered flower petals on the newlyweds. Prominent guests attend the wedding Several distinguished personalities attended the ceremony to bless the couple. Among them was Bhojpuri star Pawan Singh, who congratulated the bride and groom. Popular songs by Pawan Singh were played during the celebrations, adding to the festive atmosphere. A number of legislators and political leaders from Bihar were also present and extended their best wishes to the newly married couple. Grand wedding procession at Taj Ganges Hotel The wedding procession took place at the Taj Ganges Hotel, where Akash Deep danced enthusiastically alongside relatives and friends. The celebrations featured traditional music, with bands and drums creating a lively atmosphere as guests joined in the festivities. Around 350 people attended the wedding ceremony. Traditional Kashi rituals performed Scholars and priests from Kashi conducted the traditional 'Dwar Puja' along with special religious rituals. Following the blowing of conch shells on the stage, which was decorated around themes inspired by Kashi and Lord Shiva, chants of- Namah Parvati Pataye, Har Har Mahadev echoed throughout the venue. Venue decorated in Kashi and Shiva theme The wedding venue reflected the spiritual and cultural heritage of Kashi. From the entrance to the stage and dining area, decorations featured symbols associated with Lord Shiva and Hindu tradition, including- Elements of Kashi's culture and Indian traditions were visible throughout the venue, creating a distinctly spiritual and cultural ambience for the occasion. stories.summary: Air India's 'Easy Connect' service was launched on Thursday at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi. Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu Kinjarapu inaugurated the service following a traditional puja ceremony. The initiative is expected to make international travel significantly easier for passengers from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities such as Varanasi, Lucknow and Patna by providing seamless connections through Delhi. The service has been introduced under the Central Government's 'Hub and Spoke' aviation model. Easier access to International destinations Under the new system, passengers travelling from Varanasi to Delhi will benefit from improved connectivity to international destinations across 17 countries. These destinations include regions such as- The service is designed to provide smoother transfers and reduce the complexities typically associated with connecting international flights. Strengthening India's global air connectivity Speaking at the launch, Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu Kinjarapu described the initiative as an important step towards enhancing India's global aviation connectivity. He said the service would contribute significantly to the government's objective of developing India into an international aviation hub, in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision. According to the minister, passengers, traders, students and tourists from the Purvanchal region will particularly benefit from the improved connectivity. International travel through the Delhi hub is expected to become more convenient, while access to onward connecting flights will also improve. New boost for Purvanchal's Aviation Network Air India Station Manager Atif Idris said the Hub and Spoke model links regional cities with major aviation centres, allowing passengers to access a broader international network. According to him, the model offers- Airport Director Puneet Gupta said the initiative would strengthen air connectivity across Purvanchal and support the growth of tourism, trade and investment in the region. Senior officials attend launch event The launch programme was attended by several senior officials, including- How the hub and spoke model work? Officials said the model will be rolled out in phases across several other cities in the country. The objective is to create a more efficient, integrated and globally competitive aviation ecosystem. Under the Hub and Spoke model- Passengers from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities can complete check-in procedures for their final international destination directly at their departure airport. No need to re-check baggage at Delhi One of the key benefits of the Easy Connect service is that passengers will not need to collect and re-check their baggage at the hub airport. After arriving in Delhi, travellers can seamlessly connect to Air India's extensive international network without additional baggage formalities. Immigration clearance at the origin Airport Another major advantage is that passengers will complete their international immigration procedures at their originating airport. This means travellers will- Officials also noted that passengers will no longer face the inconvenience and unfamiliarity often associated with transiting through foreign hub airports before reaching their final destinations. The initiative is expected to make international travel simpler, faster and more accessible for passengers from regional cities across northern and eastern India.

stories.title: BHU-UG admissions to begin from the first week of July:New courses will be launched, NTA to share list of qualified students with BHU
stories.summary: Amidst the PG admission process at Banaras Hindu University (BHU), the National Testing Agency (NTA) has declared the CUET-UG 2025 results. Following this, the central admission committee has also started preparations for undergraduate (UG) admissions. It is expected that after receiving the list of qualified candidates from NTA in the next one week, the UG admission process will be started from the first week of July. In 2024, approximately 8,889 students took admission in BHU. In the last session, two new courses like BSc Radiotherapy and Radiology were introduced, and the number of seats had gone up. At the same time, seats were reduced in some courses with low demand, and new courses were also started in affiliated colleges. Last year, the university had planned admissions for about 9,200 seats, but due to delays in the admission process, many seats remained vacant. This time, the university is set to complete the admission process in a time-bound manner. Admission counseling announced 10-15 days after receiving data This year, due to the timely start of the admission process, all seats are expected to be filled. Along with the implementation of CBCS (Choice Based Credit System) since last year, BHU will also admit 15% of students in its undergraduate (research) programs. Admission Cell Coordinator Prof. Bhaskar Bhattacharya informed that technical preparations related to admissions have been completed on the BHU website. As soon as the candidates' data is received, the dates for admission counseling will be announced. This may take 10 to 15 days. 1182 paid seats will also be available in the faculties There are more than 9200 seats in undergraduate courses across various faculties, the campus-based women's college, and affiliated colleges. Approximately eight thousand regular seats are available among these. These include 3480 in the main campus, 695 in the women's college, and 3537 seats in affiliated colleges. Additionally, students will also get an opportunity for admission on 1182 paid seats.

stories.title: Climate change could transform Tamil Nadu’s Western Ghats by 2050 | Focus Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: The Western Ghats may still be green in the coming decades—but they may not be the same forests we know today. A new study by researchers from Anna University’s Centre for Climate Change and Disaster Management warns that climate change could gradually alter the composition of forests across Tamil Nadu’s Western Ghats, including the Nilgiris, Kodaikanal, Valparai, Courtallam and Kanyakumari regions. The study suggests that evergreen and deciduous forests could shrink, while drier thorn forests may expand by 2050. Such changes could affect biodiversity, water security, carbon storage and ecosystem stability across the State. In this episode of The Hindu Focus Tamil Nadu, D. Suresh Kumar explains what the findings mean, why scientists are concerned, and what the future could hold for one of India’s most important biodiversity hotspots.

stories.title: Coaching centres remain shut in Gorakhpur:Operators missing after safety inspections begin, serious lapses exposed
stories.summary: Following the devastating fire incident in Lucknow, authorities have launched inspections of safety arrangements at coaching centres across Uttar Pradesh. The impact of the crackdown is clearly visible in Gorakhpur, where many coaching institutes have remained closed for the third consecutive day. Centres that would normally be filled with hundreds of students attending classes now stand deserted. Several coaching operators have apparently chosen to shut their centres rather than face inspection. Attempts to contact them proved unsuccessful, with many mobile phones switched off and some operators declining to answer calls. This has raised an important question: why did so many coaching centres close immediately after the inspections began? Are operators trying to hide safety deficiencies? The closure of coaching centres during the inspection drive has led to concerns that some institutions may be attempting to conceal shortcomings in fire safety measures, emergency exits and other essential safety standards. To examine these concerns, the Bhaskar team conducted a ground investigation of coaching centres operating in different parts of Gorakhpur. The inspection uncovered serious safety concerns at several locations. Many centres were found operating in buildings accessed through narrow lanes and cramped staircases, potentially making safe evacuation extremely difficult during an emergency. Buddha Coaching Centre found closed When the Bhaskar team visited Buddha Coaching Centre in Hariom Nagar, the main entrance was locked. A premises that is usually crowded with students was completely empty. Efforts to contact the operator were unsuccessful, as the registered mobile number was switched off. The on-site inspection revealed that the coaching centre operates from a two-storey building and caters to approximately 50 to 60 students daily. However, the available safety arrangements appeared inadequate for the number of students attending classes. Investigators found- The most significant concern was the absence of an alternative escape route. In the event of a fire, if smoke filled the staircase or the passage became blocked, students could face serious difficulties evacuating safely. Acme Computer Education also found locked The Bhaskar team then visited Acme Computer Education in Shahi Market. This centre was also found closed, with the main gate locked. Investigators observed that the institute operates from a building accessed through narrow and confined staircases. These stairs serve as the only route for students to enter and leave the premises. In an emergency situation, this could pose a significant risk to evacuation efforts. Safety equipment not visible Around 30 students reportedly attend classes at the centre every day. Despite this, investigators did not observe- In the event of an accident, the absence of such measures could hamper rescue and relief operations. Student says closure notice gave no reason A student who arrived outside the coaching centre said she had received a message three days earlier informing her that classes would remain suspended for two days. However, no reason for the closure was provided. According to the student, she returned on the third day expecting classes to resume, only to find the centre still closed and the gates locked. Why were centres closed as soon as inspections began? Bhaskar's investigation found that several other coaching centres across the city were in a similar situation. Many institutes reportedly shut down shortly after the inspection campaign was launched. Attempts were made to contact multiple operators, but no responses were received. As a result, questions are being raised over whether institutions that fully comply with safety norms would have any reason to suspend operations during the inspection process. Risks of ignoring student safety Every day, hundreds of students attend coaching centres in pursuit of their academic goals. Parents entrust these institutions with the safety and well-being of their children. However, if coaching centres lack fundamental safety measures such as- Even a minor incident could potentially escalate into a major tragedy. Lessons from the Lucknow fire The situation emerging in Gorakhpur in the aftermath of the Lucknow fire has highlighted concerns about safety standards at educational institutions. The findings suggest that safety measures should exist not merely on paper but in practice. While administrative inspections continue, coaching centre operators are also being urged to place student safety at the centre of their operations and ensure compliance with all required safety norms.

stories.title: LDA seals Bhumi IAS among other coaching centres:Action over fire safety violations after Lucknow blaze killed 15
stories.summary: Following the death of 15 people in the Aliganj fire tragedy, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has launched inspections of coaching centres, libraries and shopping complexes across the city. A joint team of the LDA, Fire Department and police is inspecting establishments operating in violation of safety norms. The team sealed Bhumi IAS Coaching, Vidya Mandir Coaching and Drishtikon Library in Gomti Nagar after finding that they did not meet the required standards. The drive, launched on the instructions of LDA Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar, will continue for the next three weeks. Coaching centres, libraries, hotels, nursing homes, dance studios, playgroup schools and commercial complexes will be inspected. LDA officials said establishments found violating fire safety, parking and building plan norms will face immediate sealing and notice action. On Wednesday alone, 71 establishments were sealed for ignoring safety standards. These included major coaching institutes such as Allen, Gravity, Aakash, Government Exam Wala and Paramount. The LDA also issued notices to 83 building owners. See pictures related to the action Action linked to the fire tragedy A fire had broken out on June 22 in a building in Aliganj. The basement, ground floor and first floor housed a pet shop and clinic. The second floor accommodated Learning Space Library and Head Hopper Studio, which works in 3D art production and game asset outsourcing. Fifteen people working at Head Hopper Studio lost their lives in the blaze. ‘Building should be demolished without a minute’s delay’ Ram Kumar, a resident of Sitapur Road, visited the burnt building on Thursday afternoon. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, he said the tragedy was the result of government failure and official negligence. He added that had authorities acted earlier, such an incident could have been prevented. Building owners asking coaching centres to vacate Shiv Kumar Khatri of Gomti Nagar said Bhumi IAS Coaching was operating from his premises and that he had asked it to vacate two days ago. People stopping to see the burnt building The building where 15 people died has now been sealed by police. Residents and passersby continue to stop and look at the structure. Trends outlet told to vacate Officials directed the Trends outlet in Viraj Khand to vacate the premises, stating that the building had not been constructed according to approved standards. Drishtikon Library sealed in Virat Khand The LDA sealed Drishtikon Library in Virat Khand. Officials said the library was being operated from a residential property without fire safety arrangements, and commercial activities were being carried out in a residential complex. Bhumi IAS Coaching sealed in Gomti Nagar The LDA sealed Bhumi IAS Coaching Centre in Gomti Nagar, citing congested classrooms, the absence of a fire exit and a very narrow access route to the coaching centre. Vidya Mandir Coaching sealed in Viraj Khand The LDA also sealed Vidya Mandir Coaching in Viraj Khand for failing to comply with fire safety norms. Action against 19 engineers and 6 PCS officers LDA Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar said the building where the fire occurred had received approval for a residential map in 2016, but commercial construction later began on the premises. He said demolition orders issued at the time were subsequently withdrawn, though the reasons remain unclear. Action has now been taken against a total of 19 engineers and six PCS officers, including former Executive Engineers (XENs), Junior Engineers (JEs) and Assistant Engineers (AEs) posted at the time. Three to four of them have already retired. Report sent to PMO Following the Aliganj fire that claimed 15 lives and injured several others, the matter is being monitored at the highest level. The state government has sent a detailed report to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), covering rescue and relief operations, compensation for victims, FIRs, arrests, suspension of officials and the SIT investigation. The report also includes details about the causes of the incident, lapses found during the preliminary inquiry, the building’s approval and fire safety status, administrative and legal action taken so far, and measures proposed to prevent similar tragedies in future.

stories.title: Sanjay Singh submits Ram Mandir land scam evidence to SIT:AAP MP hands over 11 papers, questions delay in FIR; Kejriwal to visit Ayodhya tomorrow
stories.summary: AAP MP Sanjay Singh on Thursday submitted documents related to alleged land deal irregularities to the Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation and land purchase controversy. Singh arrived at the office of SIT Chairman Vijay Vishwas Pant in Lucknow at around 11 am and remained inside for approximately 12 minutes before handing over the documents. Sanjay Singh questions lack of arrests and FIRs Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Sanjay Singh said he had submitted 11 documents that, according to him, contain evidence linked to alleged irregularities in land transactions associated with the Ram Mandir Trust. He said- One revelation after another is coming to light. Cash recoveries have already been made and evidence relating to alleged theft from Mandir donations has surfaced. Yet no one has gone to jail so far. Why has nobody been arrested? Why has no FIR been registered? This is extremely surprising. The SIT had invited Singh to present the evidence after he publicly claimed to possess documents related to the alleged land scam. 'No route left for anyone to escape': Sanjay Singh Sanjay Singh said he had submitted original documents to the SIT and claimed that the evidence leaves little room for those involved to avoid scrutiny. According to Singh, the documents relate to the following transactions- 1. Land purchased by Trust at higher price- The Trust allegedly purchased land worth ₹4.97 crore from Harish and Kusum Pathak for ₹8 crore. Singh claimed that the witnesses to the transaction included Rishi Kumar Upadhyay and Anil Mishra. Anil Mishra is a Trust member, while Rishi Kumar Upadhyay was the BJP mayor at the time. 2. Land resold to Trust within five minutes According to Singh, in 2021 Sultan Ansari and Ravi Mohan Tiwari purchased land from Harish and Kusum Pathak and sold it to the Trust for ₹18.5 crore just five minutes later. He alleged that Anil Mishra and Rishi Kumar Upadhyay were witnesses in both transactions. 3. ₹41.60 lakh land sold for ₹2 crore- Singh alleged that a parcel of land valued at ₹41.60 lakh was sold for ₹2 crore. 4. Land bought by Rishi Upadhyay's nephew- According to Singh, Rishi Kumar Upadhyay's nephew purchased land for ₹20 lakh and sold it seven months later to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai. 5. Donated land later sold for ₹1 crore- Singh alleged that on 14 May 2020, Deep Narayan, a nephew of Rishi Kumar Upadhyay, received a piece of land as a donation and later sold it to Champat Rai for ₹1 crore. 6. Land purchased from Braj Mohan Das- According to the documents cited by Singh, on 20 May 2021, Champat Rai purchased land from Braj Mohan Das for ₹5.60 crore, although its earlier valuation was ₹92.50 lakh. 7. Land valued at ₹51.80 lakh- Singh alleged that another parcel of land valued at ₹51.80 lakh was also purchased by Champat Rai, though the final sale amount remains unclear. 8. Land valued at ₹45 lakh- He further claimed that details regarding the sale price of a ₹45 lakh land parcel remain unavailable and require investigation. 9. ₹9 crore land purchased for ₹55.47 crore- According to Singh, a land parcel worth ₹9 crore was purchased on 16 November 2023 for ₹55.47 crore. 10. ₹2.92 crore land sold for ₹24 crore- Singh alleged that on 2 April 2024, land valued at ₹2.92 crore was sold to Champat Rai for ₹24 crore. 11. Nazul land transaction questioned- Referring to official records, Singh claimed that the Ayodhya SDM had identified one of the properties as Nazul land. He questioned how such land could have been purchased for ₹24 crore and alleged that the transaction amounted to a direct misuse of donation funds collected by the Trust. Mandir Trust rejects reports of Champat Rai's resignation Meanwhile, Ram Mandir Construction In-Charge Gopal Rao dismissed reports circulating on social media that Trust General Secretary Champat Rai had resigned. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Rao said- False and misleading information is being spread on social media. People should not pay attention to rumours. The matter is being investigated by the SIT. Wait for the SIT report. The truth will become clear after that. The clarification came after several journalists and social media influencers posted claims on X on Thursday morning suggesting that Champat Rai had stepped down. Dainik Bhaskar subsequently contacted Gopal Rao and VHP National General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra, both of whom denied the reports. Bajrang Lal Bagra also stated that claims regarding Champat Rai's resignation were incorrect. Arvind Kejriwal to visit Ayodhya AAP National Convenor and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal is scheduled to arrive at Lucknow Airport before travelling to Ayodhya by road. After an overnight stay in Ayodhya, he is expected to visit the Ram Lalla Mandir on 26 June and offer prayers at Hanumangarhi. Kejriwal is also scheduled to meet several saints and religious leaders during the visit. Political observers view the visit as significant in the context of the ongoing controversy surrounding Ram Mandir donations and land transactions, as well as the broader political developments currently unfolding in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: UP BJP announces new state team ahead of assembly elections:Pooja Pal named VP, Rajnath Singh's younger son also inducted
stories.summary: Ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP on Thursday announced its new state team, comprising 64 office-bearers. Of these, 52 leaders have been included in the state executive committee. The appointments include 19 vice-presidents, 19 secretaries, 8 general secretaries and 6 presidents of party wings. In addition, the party has appointed 6 regional presidents, 3 office secretaries and 3 other office-bearers. Pooja Pal and Neeraj Singh included in state team MLA Pooja Pal, who had rebelled against the Samajwadi Party (SP), has been appointed as a state vice-president. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's younger son, Neeraj Singh, has also been inducted into the state team and appointed as a vice-president. Meanwhile, Rohit Mishra from Pratapgarh has been named president of the BJP Yuva Morcha. State Leadership Team Now Numbers 54 With Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary and Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh included, the state leadership team now consists of 54 members. The newly announced team includes 13 women. OBC representation sees significant increase Compared with the previous state executive, representation from the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category has increased substantially. The number of OBC leaders in the state team has risen from 16 to 25. Meanwhile, 21 members from the general category have been included in the new executive. Caste-wise representation in the new team The composition of the state team reflects changes across several communities. Thakur representation has reduced from 7 to 6 members. Brahmin representation has reduced from 8 to 7 members. Four Bhumihar leaders have been included. Three Vaishya leaders have been given positions. One Srivastava representative has been included. SC and ST representation Among Scheduled Caste (SC) communities, seven leaders have been included in the new state team. For Scheduled Tribe (ST) representation, Engineer Vidyabhushan Gond is the sole member to have been appointed. See full list- All six regional presidents replaced The BJP has replaced all six regional presidents across Uttar Pradesh. The new appointments are- Several outgoing regional presidents have been given new responsibilities. Former Kashi regional president Dilip Patel has been promoted and appointed state general secretary. Former Kanpur regional president Prakash Pal has been appointed state president of the BJP OBC Morcha. Former Braj regional president Dhruv Vijay Shakya has been made a state vice-president. Former Gorakhpur regional president Sahajanand Rai has been appointed a state secretary. However, former Western regional president Satyendra Sisodia and former Awadh regional president Kamlesh Mishra have not been included in the new team. Key promotions in the new team Several leaders have been elevated to higher organisational positions. Abhijat Mishra has been promoted from state secretary to state general secretary. Archana Mishra has been elevated from state secretary to state vice-president. Geeta Shakya has been promoted from Mahila Morcha state president to BJP state general secretary. Shankar Lodhi has been elevated from state secretary to state general secretary. Dilip Patel has also been appointed state general secretary following his tenure as Kashi regional president. Why is the new team significant? The new team led by Pankaj Chaudhary will shoulder full responsibility for the BJP's preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. It will also be the first Assembly election in Uttar Pradesh under the supervision of Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh. While he has prior experience handling elections in Jharkhand, this will be his first Uttar Pradesh Assembly poll in the role. The newly constituted team will be responsible for- The team will also be tasked with implementing decisions taken by the BJP's central and state leadership at the grassroots level. Political observers say that during an election year, the role of a state office-bearer carries significance comparable to that of a minister. This is one of the key reasons many former office-bearers were keen to retain their positions in the organisation.
