stories.title: Lucknow fire survivor left paralysed after jumping from building:Legs numb, ribs fractured and lungs damaged; 7 doctors fight to save him
stories.summary: Jayant Gupta, who jumped from the second floor of a building to save his life during the Lucknow fire tragedy, has been fighting for survival for the past four days. A severe spinal cord injury has left the lower half of his body numb. Jayant is undergoing treatment at King George's Medical University (KGMU), where specialists from seven departments are monitoring his condition. Severe spinal cord injury leaves legs paralysed Dr Avdhesh Yadav, a neurosurgery expert at KGMU, told Dainik Bhaskar that the road to recovery will be extremely challenging for Jayant. According to Dr Yadav- 'Jayant has fractures in both legs. His legs have become paralysed and are completely numb. This is known as a complete cord injury. The chances of recovery are very low. It remains to be seen how much improvement occurs over time.' However, the doctor expressed hope that Jayant may eventually be able to stand on his own feet again. Jayant fell directly onto an iron grille after jumping from the building. He sustained critical injuries and lost consciousness before being rushed to KGMU's Trauma Centre. See in 3 pictures how Jayant saved his life- Rib fractures and lung injuries detected Doctors said Jayant suffered multiple rib fractures. The 10th rib on the right side and the 9th rib on the left side were severely damaged, causing injuries to his lungs as well. As a result, he has been provided ICD support (Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator) and remains under observation in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Both of his hands were also badly burnt during the incident. A severe injury at the D-10 level of the spinal cord has resulted in paraplegia. Doctors also found blood accumulation around both lungs (bilateral haemothorax) along with multiple rib fractures. He was in a state of shock when admitted to hospital. MRI reveals extensive damage An MRI scan revealed a serious ligament injury in the spine between the D-9 and D-11 vertebral levels. Doctors also detected- Dr Yadav said a multidisciplinary panel of experts has been formed to oversee Jayant's treatment. The team includes specialists from- Experts from other departments will also be consulted if required. Doctors say their primary goal is to ensure Jayant receives the best possible care and recovers as quickly as possible. Treatment provided so far According to hospital officials, Jayant is receiving comprehensive medical care, including oxygen support and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Doctors have conducted- Meanwhile, the plastic surgery team is treating his burn injuries. Conscious and stable in ICU Doctors said Jayant is fully conscious and responding appropriately to medical instructions. His blood pressure and other vital parameters remain stable. He is breathing normally without assistance and does not require ventilator support. His oxygen saturation level has been recorded at 96 per cent while breathing room air. A talented animation artist Jayant had been working at Head Hopper Studio since June 2022. Over the years, he developed expertise in hard-surface 3D modelling and texturing. More recently, he had focused on character modelling for animation projects. He learned animation at MAAC India and created several notable 3D character designs, including Textured Carbine and Wonder Woman. Key facts about Jayant Jump that saved his life Jayant was working on the second floor of Head Hopper Studio when the fire broke out. As flames engulfed the building and escape routes became inaccessible, he jumped from the second floor in an attempt to save himself. He landed on an iron grille and sustained life-threatening injuries. Although he survived the blaze, all 15 people who remained trapped inside the building lost their lives.

stories.title: Suspected Ram Mandir attack plot foiled:UP man arrested in Karnataka; ATS claims links to Pakistan-based terror group
stories.summary: A suspected terrorist allegedly plotting to blow up the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was arrested by the ATS and NIA in Karnataka on Wednesday evening. The accused, identified as Mohammad Suhail (22), is a resident of Gangoh in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district and was working in a factory in Karnataka. The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) claims that Suhail had links with a Pakistan-based terrorist organisation. Investigators say he had been living in Davangere, Karnataka, while concealing his identity, although the exact manner in which he did so remains unclear. Agencies have reportedly recovered Pakistani phone numbers, suspicious WhatsApp group links, and photographs showing him with weapons from his mobile phone. Officers from the NIA and ATS are currently interrogating him, and he may soon be brought to Uttar Pradesh for further questioning. Lead emerged during interrogation of two suspected terrorists According to sources, ATS recently arrested two suspected terrorists, Zameer Khan (22) from Davangere and Alla Baksh (24) from Tumakuru. During questioning, both allegedly disclosed Suhail's name. Acting on this information, ATS launched an operation and arrested him. Preliminary investigations suggest that Suhail was in contact with Pakistani terrorists through social media platforms. What did investigators find on Suhail's mobile phone? Officials say that during interrogation, Suhail admitted discussing plans to attack the Ram Mandir. Investigating agencies claim to have recovered photographs of him posing with weapons from his mobile phone. These images have been sent for forensic examination. In addition, officers reportedly found phone numbers bearing Pakistan's country code and several audio clips. In some of these recordings, Suhail is allegedly heard discussing plans to target the Ram Mandir. Taken to Tumakuru for further interrogation Davangere Superintendent of Police (SP) Shekhar HT said intelligence agencies had already received inputs regarding Suhail's activities. Following these inputs, a joint operation was carried out by Deputy SP Basavaraj of Davangere Rural Sub-Division, the Central Intelligence Agency, and the Davangere Crime Branch team. Suhail was arrested from Bannikodu village in Davangere district and is being taken to Tumakuru for further interrogation. Suhail's father, Liaqat, said he works as a labourer and has nine children — five daughters and four sons. Suhail is the youngest among all his siblings. All five daughters are married. His eldest brother, Ayaz, works as a driver in Saudi Arabia. The second brother, Shoaib, lives at home and is currently unemployed. The third brother, Jamil, works in the hosiery industry in Delhi. Suhail is the youngest and fourth son in the family. Worked as a labourer before going to Karnataka According to Suhail's father Liaqat, he studied at a madrasa up to Year 5. He previously worked as a daily-wage labourer. On 6 June, he travelled to Karnataka through a contractor to work as a painter. Liaqat claimed that Suhail was "mentally unstable" and had a strong desire to become famous on Instagram. He added- "I do not know what happened after he went to Karnataka. stories.title: Sindhi body claims 200 kg silver handed to Champat Rai:No receipt issued yet from Ram Mandir; 'Kakabhushundi' idol also missing
stories.summary: New allegations are surfacing daily in the Shri Ram Temple offerings theft case in Ayodhya. The Vishwa Sindhi Seva Sangam of Mumbai has claimed it has not received a receipt for the 200 kg of silver it donated, nor has the trust disclosed how the silver was used. A woman has also alleged that she was not given a receipt for donating a silver idol of Kakabhushundi. Both donations were reportedly handed over to Champat Rai, the temple trust’s general secretary. Meanwhile, Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao were seen actively participating in the flag-hoisting ceremony of the Sheshavatar Temple in the complex on June 23. Their presence has fueled speculation that all three may receive a clean chit in the offerings theft case. Read this report 200 Sindhis from 15 countries had donated silver slabs Dr. Raju Manwani, Chairman of Vishwa Sindhi Seva Sangam, told Dainik Bhaskar that At the time of temple construction, the whole world was donating. The Sindhi community also decided to donate 20-25 kg of silver. However, 200 people from the Sindhi community living in more than 15 countries were ready to donate one kilogram of silver each. After collecting 200 kg of silver bricks, we contacted Champat Rai. He took the bricks and called us to Ayodhya. 200 people from the community reached Ayodhya with the bricks on January 26, 2021. After the worship of the bricks, they were handed over to Champat Rai. Dr. Raju Manwani said, All the bricks had pictures of Lord Jhulelal and other deities. Champat Rai said that after checking the purity of the bricks, a receipt would be sent. He also assured that we would be informed where the bricks would be used.Today it has been five years, but no receipt has been given by the Trust. Neither did anyone call, nor did we receive any response on our phones. After the case of theft of offerings came to light, I have received calls from many people in the community. They want to know where the donated 200 kg of silver has been used. Silver Kakabhushundi idol also missing A woman named Anita Bhardwaj has also accused them of not providing a receipt for donated silver. The woman claims that she gave a silver idol of Kakabhushundi (a sage in the form of a crow) to Champat Rai in Karsevakpuram. She had requested him to give it a place in the Ram Darbar. Champat Rai had said that cameras are not allowed inside. Photos and receipts will be sent later. After this, Anita wrote several letters to Champat Rai asking for the receipt, but she has not received it to date. She was also not told anything about that idol. 5 suspects imprisoned in Ram Mandir complex The initial investigation in the offering theft case was conducted by the Trust itself. It is being claimed that the Trust has seized approximately 2 crore rupees and jewelry from the homes and stated locations of several personnel by June 13. Since then, the suspects Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Avinash, Karunesh, and Manish Yadav have been kept within the temple premises. Their mobile phones have also been confiscated. The SIT has also interrogated them. Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, who was formerly the driver of General Secretary Champat Rai, has also been kept on the premises. However, he is allowed to move freely anywhere within the premises. He is also using a mobile phone. Whereas, Tinnu is still being described as the main figure in the offering theft case. The recovery of jewelry from his house has also come to light. The temple administrators are living in the temple premises as before. Champat Rai is also living in the temple. Earlier, he used to live in the VHP office located in Karsevakpuram. Dr. Anil Mishra is commuting from his home. All three trustees likely to get a clean chit In the offerings theft case, the roles of General Secretary Champat Rai, counting in-charge and trust member Dr Anil Mishra, and manager Gopal Rao are under scrutiny. Former temple accountant Mahipal and former engineer Dinanath Verma have alleged that Champat Rai was aware of both the theft of offerings and a 40% commission in the purchase of construction materials. They claim they informed him, but instead of taking action, both were removed from temple duties. Mumbai businessman Anil Vishwakarma has accused Champat Rai of not issuing receipts for a Dwadash Jyotirling necklace and foot-pads donated to the temple. The SIT has recorded statements from Vishwakarma and Guru Acharya Vinod Mishra, while the Indian Bullion Jewellers Association has also raised questions over 60 kg of silver bricks. During his recent visit to Ayodhya, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reportedly kept all three individuals away from official programmes. However, Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao were seen actively participating in the flag-hoisting ceremony at Sheshavatar Temple on 23 June. Champat Rai led the event and delivered a speech, fuelling claims that all three have received a clean chit in the SIT's preliminary report.

stories.title: Heavy rain in Prayagraj, alert issued for 26 districts:Temperature crosses 44°C, heat and humidity intensify
stories.summary: The spell of fluctuating weather conditions continues across Uttar Pradesh. Heavy rain accompanied by strong winds was reported in Prayagraj early on Thursday, while light drizzle occurred in Meerut. Most cities across the state witnessed bright sunshine from the morning onwards. With wind speeds remaining low, heat and humidity levels have increased significantly. Rain and heatwave alerts issued The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 26 districts and a heatwave warning for eight districts on Thursday. Strong winds with speeds of up to 60 kmph are also likely during this period. Monsoon Expected to Enter UP Within 2–3 Days There is some relief on the monsoon front, with weather officials indicating that the southwest monsoon could enter Uttar Pradesh within the next two to three days. The monsoon is expected to enter the state through the Gorakhpur-Maharajganj region via the Bihar border by 28 June. According to forecasts- Typically, the monsoon reaches Uttar Pradesh by around 20 June. This year, however, it is running approximately eight days behind schedule. The monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj for the past 15 days. Banda records highest temperature During the past 24 hours, Banda was the hottest location in the state, recording a maximum temperature of 44.2°C. Several districts experienced heavy rainfall, including- In Agra, strong winds during the evening caused a roadside utility pole to collapse onto parked cars. The rear portions of two vehicles were crushed in the incident. Lucknow Meteorological Centre scientist Atul Kumar Singh said the southwest monsoon became active over parts of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on June 23. He said the monsoon is expected to advance over the remaining parts of the North Arabian Sea, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand over the next two to three days. This could allow it to reach parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar within the next three to four days. How will the weather for the next five days ? 26 June: Dry weather is expected across eastern and western Uttar Pradesh, with temperatures likely to rise. 27 June: Heatwave conditions are expected to persist across the state. Hot winds may intensify discomfort, especially in eastern Uttar Pradesh. 28 June: Western Uttar Pradesh is likely to remain dry, while eastern districts may receive rain. 29 June: Light rain is likely in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern parts may witness heavy rainfall. 30 June: Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is expected in western Uttar Pradesh. Eastern Uttar Pradesh may experience strong storms along with widespread rainfall.

stories.title: 'Dead bodies found holding each other's hands':Firefighters recount horror inside Lucknow's deadly blaze
stories.summary: Officers, firefighters and police personnel, who were part of the rescue team in Lucknow fire tragedy, have revealed chilling details about the operation. The fire, which erupted on 22 June at Head Hopper Studio in Aliganj area, claimed 15 lives. The Bhaskar Investigation Team spoke to members of the rescue team to recount how the operation unfolded. They described the life-threatening conditions they faced, the challenges that slowed the rescue, and the haunting scenes they witnessed inside the smoke-filled building. Here's what they said: The entire building was engulfed in thick smoke. The rear wall and several windows had been blown apart. Wearing breathing apparatus, we climbed to the second floor using ropes. Inside, visibility was almost zero. Even our torchlights were ineffective. We could only move forward by instinct. The broken windowpanes allowed some of the smoke to escape, creating a narrow path for us to enter the Head Hopper Studio. What we found inside was horrifying. Every time our feet brushed against a body, we realised that someone was lying on the floor. Victims were found inside cabins and washrooms. Some bodies were slumped against walls. One person's head was bent to one side while the body had collapsed in another direction. A young man was found with his hand covering his mouth, his body leaning against a wall. It appeared he had tried to shield himself from the smoke but could not survive. First, 3 pictures of the firefighters who carried out the rescue Now read what the firefighters are saying Case 1: AC outdoor units blocked the staircase, forcing rescuers to enter from the rear A constable from Madiyaon police station, among the first to reach the spot, said the rescue operation was hampered from the very beginning. "Eight to ten AC outdoor units had been installed along the narrow staircase leading into the building. Several motorcycles and scooters parked there had also caught fire. The flames and thick smoke quickly engulfed the only entrance, making the passage even narrower." According to him, firefighters initially tried to douse the blaze from the front, but there was no way to enter the building. There were no windows or alternative openings through which rescuers could reach those trapped inside. Some firefighters climbed onto the roof by placing a ladder against the neighbouring building. They hoped to enter through the rooftop staircase, but found the access door secured with a heavy lock that could not be broken from above. With every route blocked, the rescue team decided to breach the rear wall. The building had only one entry and exit point, and that too was obstructed by AC outdoor units, making the rescue operation significantly more difficult. Case 2: A 9-inch wall stood between rescuers and the trapped victims The fireman involved in breaching the rear wall said it appeared to be the quickest way to reach those trapped inside. "The wall was around nine inches thick and reinforced with heavy plaster. It was extremely strong." A drilling machine was brought to the site, but it could not be operated because the electricity supply had already been disconnected. With no time to lose, Constable Mayank, posted at Madiyaon police station, picked up a heavy sledgehammer. "Waiting for the machine was not an option. We believed breaking the wall was the only way to save those inside. I kept striking the wall continuously until it finally gave way," he said. Once the opening was created, firefighters gained access to the building through two breaches made in the rear wall. It was through these openings that the rescue operation progressed. Later, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak visited the site to inspect the breached wall. Case 3: 'Visibility was zero; we found bodies only after stumbling over them' The first firefighter to enter the building described conditions inside as almost impossible. "When we stepped inside, nothing was visible. The smoke was so dense that even our torchlights were ineffective. We could only move forward by instinct, feeling our way with each step." He said rescuers often realised someone was lying on the floor only after their boots brushed against a body. Because of the dense smoke and the building's maze-like layout, firefighters tied themselves together with ropes before entering. "We stayed connected throughout the operation. There was a constant fear that someone from the team could lose their way inside. The ropes ensured that no one got separated." After the rear wall was breached, rescue teams entered the building and recovered 15 bodies. Case 4: Cabins became smoke traps; victims were found across the studio A firefighter involved in recovering the bodies said the second floor had been divided into multiple cabins using glass partitions. "The smoke spread into every section of the studio. We found bodies in almost every cabin. Some victims had collapsed near the doors, while others were found inside enclosed rooms." Several bodies were found lying close together. "Their hands were touching each other, almost as if they had been holding hands. It looked like a scene from a film." One young man was found sitting against a wall with his hand covering his mouth, apparently trying to protect himself from the smoke. Another victim was discovered inside a washroom. Bodies of young men and women were scattered across the studio. Case 5: 'Better ventilation could have saved lives' The police officer leading the rescue operation believes the building's design turned the fire into a deadly trap. "If the building had adequate windows, exhaust systems or proper ventilation, much of the smoke could have escaped. Perhaps many lives could have been saved." He said the structure was almost completely sealed except for the front entrance. "There were virtually no windows. The smoke remained trapped inside, making survival difficult for those trapped and preventing rescuers from reaching them quickly." Rescue operation at a glance

stories.title: Ram Mandir trust detected theft on June 4:Champat Rai kept denying it; cash-filled bag found on June 5
stories.summary: Ayodhya Ram Mandir Trust General Secretary Champat Rai already had information about the theft of offerings, but he did not take timely action against the accused. Instead, he continued to lie to people. It is being reported that on June 4, trust officials found bundles of notes in the toilet of the counting room. The bundles contained approximately three to four lakh rupees. After this, trust officials along with policemen deployed for Ram Mandir security reached the house of counting room employee Avinash Shukla. A bag was found there. CCTV footage of this has emerged. It is being claimed that the bag was filled with money. According to sources, when no concrete action was taken in the matter, some employees associated with the trust leaked information about the irregularities in offerings to the media on June 7. On the same day, first SP's former MLA Pawan Pandey and then party president Akhilesh Yadav raised this issue on X. Police have so far recovered Rs 79.85 lakh from the locations of the accused in this case. Police reached Avinash's house, he came out with a black bag According to sources, on June 5, the police team along with trust officials reached Avinash Shukla's house. He was interrogated there. Cash was also recovered from his house. After this, the police took Avinash Shukla along with them for questioning. A 24-second video of this has surfaced, which is from 8:13 PM on June 5. In the video, Avinash is seen wearing a yellow shirt. While a temple employee has a black bag in his hand. According to sources, there was money in the black bag. Police personnel are seen taking Avinash Shukla away in a white car. However, there has been no official confirmation of money being found in the bag. On June 7, Champat Rai had said - No case of theft has come to light so far Champat Rai had given clarification on Akhilesh's allegations. He had said that the Trust undergoes internal audit from time to time. Representatives of the Trust and SBI Bank are involved in this work. The audit continues for several days. The same work is going on these days. No such matter has come to light so far. Watch the VIDEO... Police conducted raids at the homes of 8 accused On Sunday, at 7 AM, 8 police teams simultaneously raided the homes of 8 accused imprisoned in the offering theft case. During this, 3 of the accused's homes were found locked. Police questioned the neighbors. The house of Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, a close associate of Champat Rai, was found locked. A raid was also conducted at the house of accused Anukalp Mishra. Documents of purchased properties and bank account details were scrutinized. Police found a diary and some important documents at Anukalp's house. Police believe that the diary is related to the Ram Mandir offering theft case. Revenue officers, especially Lekhpals (revenue clerks), were included in the raids. Police conducted investigations for about 8 hours until 3 PM. SIT submitted report on June 23, arrest made 2 days later The theft case first came to light on June 7. The UP government formed an SIT on June 13. The SIT submitted a preliminary report to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on June 23. On June 25, the first FIR was registered based on a complaint by trust member Krishna Mohan. In this, 8 people including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu were named. However, the names of other senior officials including Champat Rai and Dr. Anil Mishra are not included. Just hours after the FIR was registered, police arrested 8 accused including Tinnu. On Friday, the CJM court sent all the accused to jail for three days. On Friday itself, temple trust general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr. Anil Mishra resigned. Know how Ram Mandir theft was exposed It is being said that the sevadars (temple servants) were aware of the embezzlement going on in the temple for years. Due to big names being involved in this, they were not speaking up. In the last 2 years, as Tinnu's dominance increased, it started bothering a faction working in the temple. This faction made a plan and developed closeness with him. Then after finding out all the facts, they passed this information to the media.

stories.title: Trainee pilot caught in aircraft propeller in Kanpur, seriously injured:Accident while getting off plane during night flying session; trainer removed
stories.summary: A major negligence came to light during night flying training at Kanpur Airport. On the night of June 26 (Friday), a twin-engine aircraft landed safely. However, the trainee pilot got down from the aircraft even before the engine was shut off. Due to this, she came in the way of the rotating propeller (fan). She suffered serious injuries to her back in the accident. The staff present at the spot took her to the hospital, where treatment is ongoing. After the incident, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has started an investigation. Along with this, the flight instructor has been removed from training duty. Know the complete matter Garg Aviation Flying Training Organization (FTO)'s Tecnam P2006T (VT-NBV) aircraft was on night instructional flying. It had one flight instructor and one trainee pilot on board. The aircraft had landed safely on the runway. However, the engine was running and both propellers were rotating. During this time, the trainee pilot got down from the aircraft. Due to this, she came directly into the path of the moving propeller. DGCA has removed the flight instructor Taking the incident seriously, DGCA has removed the concerned flight instructor from training duty until the investigation is completed. Apart from this, the Tecnam P2006T (VT-NBV) aircraft involved in the accident has also been grounded until the investigation is completed. Meanwhile, Chakeri Airport Director Pradeep Yadav refused to comment on this incident. DGCA will determine responsibility after investigation report According to aviation experts, passengers or trainees are only allowed to disembark from any aircraft when the engine is completely shut down and the propeller has completely stopped. In such a case, initially this accident points towards human error, negligence in the training process, or violation of safety protocols. DGCA has said that a detailed investigation of the entire incident is being conducted. Responsibility will be determined based on the investigation report. If necessary, action will be taken against the concerned individuals and the training institute as per rules.

stories.title: UP Home Guard recruitment results declared, 1.07 lakh candidates qualify:Will undergo document screening and physical test for 41,424 vacant posts
stories.summary: The result of the UP Home Guard recruitment-2025 written examination was released on Sunday afternoon. This examination was held on 25, 26, and 27 April 2026 for recruitment to a total of 41,424 posts. Now the passed candidates will have to undergo document verification and physical test. The list of candidates eligible for document verification and physical test has also been released. Along with this, the category-wise cut-off list for all districts has also been issued. According to the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board, approximately 2.6 times more candidates have passed compared to the total vacancies. Date for document verification and physical test will be announced soon More than 19 lakh candidates participated in the examination held for a total of 41 thousand 424 posts. Out of these, 1 lakh 07 thousand 221 candidates have passed. In this way, approximately 2.6 times more candidates compared to the vacant posts have been called for document verification and physical test. Additional Secretary/Examination Controller of the Recruitment Board, Satyarth Aniruddh Pankaj, informed that the dates for document verification and physical test will be announced soon on the board's official website. stories.title: Man murdered 18 months after eloping with friend's sister:Gonda victim's throat slit, two booked in FIR
stories.summary: In Gonda, a young man was murdered by slitting his throat over a grudge related to a love marriage. The young man had eloped with and married the accused's sister about one and a half years ago. According to police, the girlfriend's brother called the young man through a common friend and killed him with a knife during a dispute while drinking alcohol. After the incident that occurred late Saturday night in Chilmapur village under Wazirgang police station area, both the accused fled. Police have registered an FIR against two people based on the complaint filed by the deceased's mother and have started searching for them. Know the complete matter in detail... Azad Singh (30), a resident of Purwa village in Wazirganj police station area, worked in a private job. His family includes mother Sheela Singh, younger brother Monu Singh, wife Pinky Singh, and four-month-old daughter Anamika. Azad's mother and younger brother live in Amritsar, while Azad lived with his wife and daughter in the Nawabganj area. According to police, about one and a half years ago, Azad had eloped with and married Pinky Singh, the stepsister of his friend and paternal uncle (relation-wise) Sandeep Singh. After this incident, a panchayat was held in the village and Azad's family was socially boycotted. Following this, his mother Sheela Singh had also separated him from the household. Azad had started living with his wife Pinky in a rented house near Nawabganj Mandi. Pinky stated that on Saturday evening around 7 PM, Suresh Vishwakarma, a resident of the village, had called Azad out from home and taken him away. About two hours later, she received information about her husband's murder. According to police, on the night of the incident, Azad had come to attend a program in Chilmapur village with his companion Suresh Vishwakarma. Before going to the program, both stopped in the village itself. During this time, Suresh mentioned drinking alcohol. Just then, Pinky's stepbrother Sandeep Singh arrived there. A dispute started between Sandeep and Azad over eloping with his sister and marrying her. It is alleged that during this, Sandeep attacked Azad's throat with a knife. Seriously injured, Azad died on the spot. After the incident, the accused fled. Ghanshyam Pandey, a resident of Chilmapur village, said that the murder took place right in front of his house. At the time of the incident, an invitation ceremony was going on in the village, which he had attended with his family. While returning, people told him that a person was lying in front of his house. Ghanshyam said that initially he thought someone was lying drunk, but when he went closer, he saw the person was soaked in blood. After this, he immediately called Dial 112. As soon as the information was received, the police reached the spot. ASP West Radheshyam Rai said- Police reached the spot on receiving information about the body and sent it for post-mortem. Based on the complaint of the deceased's mother, an FIR has been registered against Sandeep Singh, who is related as an uncle, and Suresh Vishwakarma of the village. The accused are being searched for and they will be arrested soon.

stories.title: Pravin Togadia slams Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft:Says faith of devotees has been betrayed; calls for fast-track trial capital punishment
stories.summary: The alleged donation theft case linked to the Ayodhya Ram Mandir has taken a fresh political turn, with Antarrashtriya Hindu Parishad founder Dr Pravin Togadia launching a scathing attack over the incident and demanding the strictest possible punishment for those accused. The controversy, which surfaced on June 7, has triggered widespread outrage among devotees. After the first FIR was registered on June 25 on the complaint of temple trust member Krishna Mohan, eight accused, including Ramshankar Yadav aka Tinnu, were arrested. A day later, the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) court remanded the accused to three days' judicial custody. Amid the developments, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust confirmed on Saturday that General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra had resigned. 'This is not theft of money, but an assault on the faith of crores' Addressing the foundation day function of the Antarrashtriya Hindu Parishad in Ahmedabad, Dr Togadia said, “The alleged embezzlement of temple offerings amounted to a betrayal of the faith of millions of Hindus”. He demanded that the case be heard by a fast-track court and urged the judiciary to impose the death penalty on those found guilty. He stated, “This is not merely a case of financial irregularity. It is the murder of the faith of crores of devotees.” 'Millions stood with the Ram Mandir movement' Recalling the Ram Mandir movement, Togadia said, “Millions of Hindus had joined the campaign over four decades in response to the movement's call. Countless volunteers had made personal sacrifices, while many had even laid down their lives for the construction of the temple”. He added, “People sacrificed their careers, families and even their lives for this cause. That faith has now been ridiculed.” 'Every Hindu's faith has been shaken' Togadia added, “The alleged theft continued for nearly two years and involved multiple people. The issue had deeply hurt the sentiments of devotees. This is not about the value of the donations. Every Hindu's heart has been broken. We dedicated our youth and our lives to this movement. Today that devotion has been insulted.” Calls for death penalty within two months Stepping up his attack, Togadia demanded that the trial be completed within two months through a fast-track court and that the harshest punishment be awarded if the accused are convicted. He appealed for swift legal action saying, “It was essential to restore public faith in the institution and uphold the sanctity of the temple”. Donation theft probe gathers pace The alleged donation theft case came to light on June 7, following which the Uttar Pradesh government constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) on June 13. The SIT submitted its preliminary findings to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on June 23. Based on a complaint filed by trust member Krishna Mohan, the first FIR was registered on June 25, naming eight accused, including Ramshankar Yadav aka Tinnu. The resignations of Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra were confirmed by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust on Saturday. Who is Dr Pravin Togadia? Dr Pravin Togadia is a cancer surgeon by profession and the founder-president of the Antarrashtriya Hindu Parishad (AHP). He earlier served as the International Working President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and was actively associated with the Ram Mandir movement. Having joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) at a young age, he later parted ways with the VHP in 2018 following differences with its leadership and subsequently launched the Antarrashtriya Hindu Parishad.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath tells Akhilesh Yadav to visit Ram Mandir:Says, 'If you're religious, speak openly on Mathura-Vrindavan'
stories.summary: CM Yogi launched a major attack on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav in Hathras on Sunday. He said, “I was reading one of his statements. He was saying that when his government comes, they will make Ayodhya a religious city. Hey, what will you make? You had ordered firing on Ram devotees. Today when Ayodhya is reminiscent of Treta Yuga due to the hard work of Ram devotees, your mouth has started watering.” The CM said, “Forget it. You had stopped Krishna Janmashtami celebrations in police stations and jails. You had banned the Kanwar Yatra. More than 22 temples in Hathras have been beautified. Could this have happened under the SP government? In your time, money used to go for graveyard boundaries. That's what we have diverted towards temples.” Yogi said - Akhilesh ji, you leave the worries of Ayodhya. Repent. Just have darshan of Ram Lalla once. You will gain wisdom. If you are really trying to show yourself as religious, then speak openly about Mathura-Vrindavan. Speak about Krishna Janmabhoomi. A campaign for the liberation of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi should be run on the lines of the Ram Janmabhoomi liberation movement. Respect should be given. The CM said, “Our government is engaged in providing basic facilities to the people. But you have no agenda other than kneeling before Mulla-Maulvi. Don't do the work of throwing dust. Don't prove the saying 'a frustrated cat scratches the pillar.” The CM was speaking after the inauguration and foundation laying of 143 development projects worth Rs 548 crore in Hathras. Key points from Yogi's address- 1. No hooliganism, no curfew in 9 years Yogi said, “Where there is no security, there is unrest, there are riots, curfew remains for months, development cannot even be imagined there. This was the situation before 2017. The Jawaharbagh incident in Mathura, the Kosikalan riot, the riots in Meerut-Aligarh, the Muzaffarnagar riots are examples of this. Youth had to lose their jobs. The state was defamed. Now in 9 years, no hooliganism, no curfew.” 2. 12,000 Muharram processions took place; no riots, no disturbances Yogi said, “Now there are no disturbances on the roads in the name of Muharram. Earlier, people walking on the roads were attacked in the name of sword-wielding. In the name of tazias, poor people's huts were removed. Someone's balcony was broken. High-tension wires were removed.” “The government made a new arrangement. You reduce the size of the tazia. It is not necessary that a poor person's house be removed. The balcony will not be broken. High-tension wires will not be removed. If you make it tall, you will come under the current of the high-tension line,” he added. 3. Earlier one had to face rejections everywhere for gas connection The CM said, “In the Congress and SP government, one had to face rejections everywhere to get a gas cylinder connection. Our government gives free gas to Ujjwala Yojana beneficiaries twice a year. When good governments come, development also happens. Welfare of the poor also happens. Youth also get employment. Steps are taken for women's self-reliance. Work is done to bring prosperity in the lives of farmers. All this is happening because of your one decision. You press the lotus button. In return, development happens. Security is provided. Job guarantee is provided.” 4. Will ensure better prices for potato farmers' produce Yogi said, “Hathras is now connected to the mainstream of development. Industrial investment is happening rapidly. Processing centers are being established. This will ensure potato farmers get better prices for their produce. The problem of cold storage will be resolved. An international potato center has been approved in Agra, which will provide farmers with better quality seeds. Production will increase.” 5. Congress strangled the Constitution, today SP stands with it Yogi, referring to the Emergency imposed on June 25, 1975, accused Congress of strangling the Constitution. He said that opposition leaders were sent to jail at that time. The Samajwadi Party today stands with Congress, supporting that same history. 6. Earlier development was considered limited only to Saifai He said, “Earlier development was considered limited only to Saifai, whereas in the double engine government, all 75 districts of the state are developing equally. The government is working not with appeasement, but with the goal of delivering benefits of schemes to the person standing in the last row.” 7. Will ensure budget for bus stand and medical college Yogi said, “The Hathras visit was originally proposed for June 23, but the program had to be postponed due to a tragic incident. Referring to the demands of public representatives, he also assured to provide necessary funds for solving problems related to bus stand and medical college.”

stories.title: Constable who called police officers bribe-takers dismissed:Says, 'Rewarded for speaking the truth'
stories.summary: Constable Sunil Kumar Shukla, who had referred to senior police officers as "black Englishmen" while alleging corruption within the police department, was dismissed from service on Sunday. Shukla had released a video accusing police officials of corruption, claiming that the department was being run by "black Englishmen" and that money was allegedly extorted from personnel in exchange for duty assignments at the police lines. His allegations triggered a stir within the department, following which the Police Commissioner constituted an inquiry committee on May 7, 2026. According to the committee's findings, Shukla failed to produce any concrete evidence to support his claims. Reacting to his dismissal, the former constable said, "Today I have received the reward for speaking the truth." Now know what was said in the inquiry committee's report? According to the inquiry committee, Constable Sunil made baseless allegations publicly against senior officers, which affected the image of the department. Along with this, he promoted indiscipline in the police force by using disrespectful language towards officers. He could not present any evidence before the inquiry officers either. The departmental inquiry also revealed that he used social media without departmental permission, which is a violation of the provisions of Uttar Pradesh Social Media Policy-2023, Rules 3, 6, 7 and 27 of the Uttar Pradesh Government Servants Conduct Rules-1956 and the Uttar Pradesh Uniform Regulations. Dismissal on Proven Serious Misconduct - Police Commissionerate The Police Commissionerate stated that Sunil Kumar Shukla has been dismissed from service upon proven serious misconduct. The department clarified that strict action will continue in cases of violation of discipline, service rules, and social media policy. Now know what were the constable's allegations? Constable Sunil Kumar Shukla, posted in Lucknow, had made serious allegations of corruption and illegal extortion against department officials, especially IPS officers. He posted a video on Facebook demanding that the Chief Minister conduct an impartial investigation into the entire matter. Sunil had released 3 videos on May 7, May 8, and May 10. After the videos surfaced, Sunil was sent on 20 days' leave. Along with this, 12 police personnel posted in the counting branch of the Police Lines were removed. Sunil's allegation was that illegal extortion is carried out every month from police personnel in the name of posting duty at the Reserve Police Lines. According to him, approximately two thousand rupees per month are collected from constables and head constables through the guard commander. The counting in-charge, RI, and other officers are involved in this system, and the extorted money is passed on to officers from bottom to top. The constable had said that 110 to 120 guards are deployed in a data section of Lucknow Commissionerate, while 500 to 550 duties are assigned there. According to him, approximately 400 police personnel are extorted for two thousand rupees each every month, resulting in a collection of about 8 lakh rupees. He had alleged that such extortion is also being carried out at other places. Had appealed to Chief Minister for justice In the video, Sunil had demanded Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to intervene and conduct an impartial investigation. He had said that there is no hope of getting justice from within the police department, therefore the government should take direct action. Everyone wants Bhagat Singh but no one wants him in their own home - Sunil 2015 batch constable Sunil had told Dainik Bhaskar - The Police Act of 1861 is still running with the same mentality. Earlier there were white Englishmen, now there are our own people. When your own people exploit you, it hurts more. I have no personal enmity with anyone, but there should be improvement in the system. I am the only male member of the family. I have a mother, an unmarried sister, a wife and two daughters. But if I don't raise my voice against wrong, then what is the meaning of living? Everyone respects Bhagat Singh, but doesn't want him in their own home.

stories.title: Gorakhpur police destroy 9.8 kg of narcotics:Drugs recovered in 8 cases across multiple police stations worth Rs 74.97 lakh
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Police on Saturday destroyed 9.891 kilograms of narcotics recovered in eight cases registered at different police stations across the city. The action was carried out under Operation Dahan, a campaign being conducted on the instructions of the Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP). The estimated market value of the destroyed narcotics was Rs 74.97 lakh. The contraband was disposed of using a high-capacity incinerator at M/s Medical Pollution Control Committee in Khalilabad. Ganja and smack destroyed According to the police, the destroyed narcotics included 9.540 kilograms of ganja and 351 grams of smack, recovered in eight cases registered at the Cantt, Gida, Chauri Chaura, Shahpur and Sahjanwa police stations. The estimated market value of the seized narcotics was around Rs 74.97 lakh. The disposal was carried out through the high-capacity incinerator at M/s Medical Pollution Control Committee in Khalilabad, in compliance with environmental and safety standards. Narcotics worth Rs 86.25 lakh destroyed earlier Police said that on 30 March 2026, they had also destroyed narcotics recovered in 16 cases, including 63.8 kilograms of ganja, 140 grams of charas, 20 grams of smack and 7 grams of heroin. The estimated value of those seized narcotics was around Rs 86.25 lakh. 73.858 kg of narcotics destroyed so far this year According to the SP (Crime), a total of 73.858 kilograms of narcotics have been destroyed so far in 2026, with an estimated market value of around Rs 1.61 crore. He added that the campaign against illegal narcotics will continue.

stories.title: Govt school students in Varanasi to receive grade-based report cards:Three stars on result indicate your child among the top performers
stories.summary: Children studying in schools under the Basic Education Department will now receive grades instead of marks on their report cards. The better a child's performance, the more stars they will be awarded. Until now, pupils in council schools were assessed through marks based on their performance. Under the new format, learning levels have been divided into three categories, represented by stars and inspired by elements of nature. The three categories are Sky, Mountain and Stream. Students will be assessed and placed in one of these categories according to their learning level and comprehension abilities. Understanding the three categories Sky category – Three stars Students with the highest level of performance will be placed in the Sky category and awarded three stars. This indicates that the child has achieved the highest learning level expected for their class and age. They are considered open-minded like the sky and display confidence in their abilities. Mountain category – Two stars Students with a moderate level of performance will be placed in the Mountain category and awarded two stars. This signifies that the student's progress is steady and strong. They have understood the concepts well and are progressing towards success. Stream category – One star Students who are at the initial stage of learning will be placed in the Stream category and awarded one star. This means the child has begun learning but still needs to develop greater depth and fluency in the subject. New report card format to be introduced this session Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) Bhupendra Singh said that council schools will issue report cards in the new format from the current academic session. The format has already been received from the department headquarters, and teachers will also be trained to implement the new assessment system. The report card will maintain a record of each student's performance throughout the academic year. It will separately record grades for the first term, half-yearly examination, second term and annual examination. All report cards will now be prepared using this new format.

stories.title: Gas cylinder delivery rules revised- Subsidy to stop without e-KYC:Second cylinder booking now allowed after 25 days instead of 21
stories.summary: The Central Government has introduced a series of new rules for domestic and commercial LPG consumers from June 1. The changes include stricter booking norms, mandatory OTP verification for cylinder delivery, compulsory e-KYC for subsidy beneficiaries, and tighter monitoring of piped natural gas (PNG) connections. The new regulations are aimed at curbing black marketing, improving transparency and ensuring that subsidies reach eligible beneficiaries. Under the revised rules, consumers in urban areas can now book a second 14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder only after 25 days, compared with 21 days earlier. In rural areas, the waiting period has been increased to 45 days before a second cylinder can be booked. OTP verification mandatory for cylinder delivery Receiving a domestic LPG cylinder will now require OTP verification. After booking a cylinder, an OTP will be sent to the customer's registered mobile number. The customer must provide this OTP to the delivery executive at the time of delivery. Simply showing the booking receipt will no longer be sufficient. The cylinder will only be handed over after successful OTP verification, a move intended to prevent hoarding and black marketing. e-KYC now essential to receive LPG subsidy Customers covered under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana must complete e-KYC to continue receiving the LPG subsidy. Biometric Aadhaar verification must be completed by June 30, 2026. Failure to do so will result in the subsidy being discontinued. Connections that remain unverified for an extended period may also be blocked. The Centre has also reduced the number of subsidised cylinders available under the scheme. Earlier, beneficiaries received a subsidy of ₹300 on nine cylinders annually. From June 2026, the subsidy will be available on only four cylinders per year. The subsidy amount will continue to be transferred directly to the bank account linked with the customer's e-KYC. Two simple ways to complete e-KYC 1. Through the mobile app Customers must also install UIDAI's Aadhaar FaceRD app, as face authentication cannot be completed without it. Once the process is complete, a confirmation SMS will be sent. 2. At the gas agency Customers can also visit their gas agency with- Agency staff will complete biometric verification using a fingerprint authentication device. PNG users must return their LPG cylinders According to the Ministry of Petroleum, many households continue to book LPG cylinders even after obtaining a PNG connection. Under the new rules, consumers who receive a PNG connection must surrender their LPG cylinders within 30 days of the PNG connection being activated. In return, they will receive a transfer voucher. If they later move to an area where PNG is unavailable, they can use this voucher to obtain an LPG connection again. The government has also tightened PNG compliance. If a customer fails to pay their PNG bill for two consecutive months, the connection may be disconnected without prior notice. A reconnection fee will be payable to restore supply. If inspection teams find damage to pipelines or valves caused by customer negligence during physical inspections, the repair costs will be borne by the customer. Three important questions about LPG refilling What are the rules for migrant workers? Migrant workers who frequently relocate often face difficulties providing address proof. Such consumers can obtain a 5 kg LPG cylinder from any authorised gas agency by producing their Aadhaar card. No address verification is required. What should consumers do if delivery is delayed or refused? Customers can call the LPG helpline on 1800-233-3555 or lodge an online complaint through Mylpg.in or the website of their respective gas company. Can consumers change their gas agency? Yes. Under the LPG portability scheme, consumers can switch dealers without requiring a No Objection Certificate (NOC) or paying any additional fee. The request can be submitted online through the gas company's website or mobile app after selecting a preferred dealer. Use only ISI-certified equipment The government has advised consumers to use only ISI-certified gas stoves, regulators and pipes. If an LPG-related accident or explosion occurs, affected families are eligible for accidental insurance coverage of up to ₹50 lakh, provided the stove, regulator and pipe are ISI-marked and registered with the gas agency. Commercial LPG deliveries now require DAC verification The delivery process for 19 kg commercial LPG cylinders has also changed. Customers must now provide a Delivery Authentication Code (DAC) after receiving the cylinder. Similar to an OTP, delivery will only be completed after the DAC is verified. Consumers are advised not to share the DAC before taking delivery. Once delivery is completed, customers will receive a digital cash memo containing complete payment and delivery details. Keeping the registered mobile number updated is therefore essential. LPG distributor Upendra Shukla said there is no fixed limit on the purchase of 19 kg commercial cylinders. Hotels, restaurants, dhabas and other commercial establishments can continue ordering cylinders according to their requirements. However, oil marketing companies will now closely monitor consumption patterns. Domestic LPG prices up ₹89 in three months Domestic LPG prices have risen sharply over the past three months. On June 6, the price of a domestic cylinder increased by ₹29, following an earlier ₹60 increase on March 7. This has taken the total increase to ₹89 within three months. Commercial LPG cylinders have also become more expensive. Prices were raised by ₹42 on June 1, taking the cost of a 19 kg cylinder to approximately ₹3,113. Earlier increases included ₹100 in May, ₹195.50 in April, and ₹114.50 in March, significantly increasing operating costs for hotels, restaurants and other commercial users.

stories.title: Houses of 8 accused raided in Ram Mandir theft case:Tinnu Yadav's house found locked; neighbours questioned
stories.summary: Police carried out simultaneous raids at the homes of the eight accused arrested in the Ram Mandir offering theft case at around 7 am on Sunday. Eight police teams searched the accuseds' residences at the same time. During the operation, three of the houses were found locked, following which officers questioned neighbours and gathered information about the accused. Tinnu's house found locked The residence of Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, considered a close associate of Champat Rai, was found locked when police arrived. A short while later, Tinnu's mother reached the house and opened the door, allowing officers to carry out a search inside the premises. Police then searched the nearby residence of Tinnu's nephew, accused Manish Yadav, but found that house locked as well. The house of another accused, Subhash Chandra Srivastava, was also locked, and no one was present when police arrived. Documents and bank details under scrutiny A heavy police presence remained outside the residence of accused Anukalp Mishra while search operations continued inside. Police examined documents related to properties allegedly purchased by the accused, scrutinised bank account details and recorded statements from family members. Revenue officials, particularly Lekhpal (revenue officers), also participated in the raids. Eight arrested after FIR The eight accused, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were arrested after an FIR was registered on June 25 based on a complaint filed by Ram Mandir Trust member Krishna Mohan. On June 26, the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) court remanded all eight accused to three days of judicial custody.

stories.title: Massive fire at cold storage in Lucknow:50 homes evacuated; blaze still raging after six hours, reignites due to wood and sawdust
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a cold storage facility in Lucknow at around 6:30 am on Sunday. Thick plumes of smoke were visible from nearly 4 kilometres away. Around 15 fire engines and two hydraulic platforms have been deployed to bring the blaze under control. About six hours into the rescue operation, the fire flared up again with renewed intensity. As a precautionary measure, police evacuated around 50 houses in the nearby Dayal Residency colony. The cold storage facility is located along the Lucknow–Ayodhya Highway in the Chinhat police station area. 35-year-old cold storage used to store grocery items The nearly 35-year-old Himalayan Cold Storage is currently used to store grocery items, including turmeric, chilli and other provisions. A section of the premises also contained wood and sawdust. The owner of the facility, Rahul Gupta, also reached the spot after being informed about the incident. Fortunately, no casualties have been reported so far. Chilli smoke hampers firefighting efforts Smoke from the stored chillies and spices has made firefighting operations extremely difficult. Fire brigade personnel initially attempted to enter the building, but were forced to retreat after coughing due to the intense chilli-laden smoke. Rescue and firefighting operations are continuing from the tin roof and with the help of hydraulic platforms. See 7 pictures-

stories.title: Heavy rain hits 10 UP cities, thunderstorm alert for 20:Tree falls in Fatehpur, 1 killed; monsoon expected within two days
stories.summary: Weather conditions continue to fluctuate across Uttar Pradesh. Light rain was recorded on Sunday morning in Lucknow, Maharajganj and Sambhal, bringing some relief from the heat as cool winds swept across these areas. Cloudy skies have also been reported in Prayagraj, Agra, Barabanki, Sitapur, Hardoi and neighbouring districts, with spells of sunshine breaking through intermittently. Earlier, on Saturday night, heavy rain lashed Lucknow, Kanpur, Barabanki, Unnao, Fatehpur, Jalaun and Bahraich. Strong, cool winds brought a noticeable change in the weather. In Fatehpur, a tree was uprooted during a storm and fell onto a road. A motorcyclist collided with the fallen tree, killing one youth and injuring another. Despite the scattered rainfall, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for thunderstorms, rain and lightning in 20 cities on Sunday. A heatwave warning remains in force for 61 districts. According to the IMD, the progress of the southwest monsoon has slowed for the time being. People may have to wait another one or two days before widespread relief from the heat arrives. Monsoon rainfall is expected to begin across the state on or after June 30. Even in areas that do not receive rain immediately, cloud cover is expected to persist, leading to a fall in temperatures of 8°C to 9°C. Weather systems becoming active for monsoon's arrival Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh from the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said- The weather pattern has changed across Uttar Pradesh. If easterly winds continue to prevail, the southwest monsoon could enter the state through eastern Uttar Pradesh within the next one to two days. The monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj on the Uttar Pradesh border for the past 16–17 days. Normally, it reaches the state by around June 20, but this year its advance has been delayed by approximately 9–10 days. Prayagraj hottest city in state at 43.2°C During the past 24 hours, Prayagraj recorded the highest maximum temperature in Uttar Pradesh at 43.2°C. Other maximum temperatures recorded were- Fatehpur: 42.6°C Varanasi: 42.5°C Banda: 42.6°C 5-day weather forecast June 29- Light rain is likely in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern Uttar Pradesh is expected to receive heavy rainfall. June 30- Western Uttar Pradesh is likely to witness rain accompanied by thunder and lightning. Strong thunderstorms and heavy rain are expected in eastern Uttar Pradesh. July 1- Light showers are forecast in western Uttar Pradesh. Eastern Uttar Pradesh is likely to experience thunderstorms and heavy rain, bringing relief from the heat. July 2- Light rain is expected to begin across western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern parts of the state may witness thunderstorms accompanied by rain. July 3- Widespread rainfall is expected across Uttar Pradesh. Eastern Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rain, with a significant reduction in temperatures and relief from the ongoing heat.

stories.title: 13 labourers kept like animals inside UP's factory:Stabbed with spears and beaten until they could no longer hear or think clearly
stories.summary: In an era when India has reached Mars, the idea that people could still be held captive and forced into bonded labour seems unimaginable. The obvious answer would be no. Yet, a shocking case uncovered in Uttar Pradesh's Muzaffarnagar suggests otherwise. For nearly one and a half years, 13 labourers were allegedly confined inside a disposable plate factory and subjected to brutal torture. They were fed only bran rotis with salt and chillies thrown onto the ground. Anyone who demanded to return home was allegedly beaten mercilessly with belts, screwdrivers and sharp spears. When police rescued the labourers on June 22, the injuries on their bodies and the fear in their eyes reflected months of relentless abuse. Many said they never believed they would leave the factory alive. The labourers were guarded by three armed men and two Pitbull dogs. Police also took the dogs into custody, noting that they appeared healthier than the workers they had been guarding. An FIR has been registered against factory owner Ankit Baliyan, his father Pramod Baliyan and supervisor Shiva Tyagi. Pramod and Shiva have been arrested, while Ankit remains absconding. This is the story of how the labourers were lured into the factory and trapped in what investigators describe as a system of bonded labour and systematic torture. Not a factory, but a 'Private Prison' The story began around two years ago when 27-year-old Ankit Baliyan established a disposable leaf plate and bowl manufacturing unit in Mandi village under Titawi police station limits, about 19 kilometres from Muzaffarnagar district headquarters. The factory operated under the name ‘Kisan Sarkar House’. Ankit's father, Pramod Baliyan, reportedly owns nearly 90 bighas of agricultural land and is considered an influential figure in the village. The family's political background is also significant. Pramod's father, Rajbir Singh, was shot dead in 2010. Later that year, Rajbir's widow, Sudesh Baba, was elected village Pradhan. She subsequently lost two elections, and the family was reportedly preparing to contest the upcoming village polls again this year. Ankit appointed Shiva Tyagi, a resident of Ukawali village in Budhana, as the factory supervisor. CCTV cameras were installed throughout the premises, Pitbull dogs were brought in for security, and the entire facility was designed in a manner that investigators say resembled a private prison rather than a manufacturing unit. Labourers recruited from Delhi, victims came from six states Rather than employing local workers, Ankit and Shiva allegedly travelled regularly to railway stations, bus terminals and labour markets in Delhi. According to police, they specifically targeted vulnerable people who had lost their jobs, were struggling financially or had little family support. They allegedly promised a monthly salary of ₹12,000, free accommodation, two meals a day and tea three times daily. The work, they claimed, involved only manufacturing disposable plates and bowls. The promise attracted workers from Bihar, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and Uttar Pradesh. Police also rescued one Nepali national from the factory. The labourers later told investigators that after being picked up in Delhi, they were made to consume alcohol during the journey. By the time they regained consciousness, they found themselves locked inside the factory. Most of them did not even know which district they had been taken to. Survivors describe months of brutal torture 'They beat me until my eardrum burst' Jagdish Kumar from Sitapur said Ankit brought him to the factory from Delhi about 11 months ago. He said he was forced to start working immediately. Although he had been promised an eight-hour shift, he was made to work continuously, day and night. One day, when he said he was too exhausted to continue working, he was beaten across his entire body with belts. According to Jagdish, the repeated assaults over 11 months ruptured one of his ears. While recounting his ordeal, he reportedly broke down in tears while showing police his damaged ear. 'They stabbed us with spears' Ramu, a resident of Nainital in Uttarakhand, spent nearly 80 days inside the factory. He alleged that upon arrival, his Aadhaar card and other identity documents were burned, while his mobile phone was confiscated. During those 80 days, he said, the workers were never served vegetables or lentils. Instead, they survived on bran rotis accompanied only by salt and chillies. Whenever anyone slowed down because of exhaustion, the supervisors allegedly jabbed them with sharp spears. "The blood would keep flowing, but we were never allowed to stop working," he told police. 'They threatened to throw our bodies into the forest' Sonu Chauhan, a Class 12 pass from Agra, said he was brought to the factory six months ago after being approached outside Delhi Railway Station. According to Sonu, three armed men constantly monitored the labourers. All carried pistols or firearms. He alleged they repeatedly threatened the workers, saying they would kill them, dump their bodies in the forest and leave vultures to feed on them if anyone refused to work or attempted to escape. 'They wanted to break our minds' A Nepali labourer, who had reportedly been confined for nearly 18 months, said there was not a single day when the workers escaped physical assault. ‘We were treated worse than animals,’ he reportedly told investigators. Dilshad, from Amroha, claimed the accused deliberately avoided injuring the workers' hands and legs because they needed them to keep working. Instead, they allegedly targeted the head, ears and back using sticks, hammers and any object they could find. He alleged the repeated blows to the head were intended to mentally break the workers into submission. According to him, many labourers suffered hearing loss because of repeated attacks to their ears, while marks from spear wounds remained visible on their backs. Why couldn't they escape? The obvious question is why none of the 13 labourers managed to escape earlier. Police identified three major reasons. First, Ankit, Pramod and Shiva reportedly remained inside the factory around the clock and were armed with pistols. Second, the factory stood in an isolated area surrounded by forests and fields. It was enclosed by an eight-foot boundary wall topped with two feet of electrified iron wiring. Third, only two of the factory's three gates were used, and both were guarded by Pitbull dogs roaming freely inside the premises. The labourers were repeatedly warned that if they attempted to flee, the dogs would tear them apart. Many also said they had no idea where they were being held, making escape even more difficult. Escape that led to the rescue Wrapped Himself in a Tarpaulin to Fool the Dogs Vikram, a labourer from Jodhpur in Rajasthan, eventually decided that someone had to escape if the others were ever to be rescued. The workers concluded that if at least one person could reach the police, the rest might survive. They identified an Ashoka tree growing close to the boundary wall as their only possible escape route. On the night of June 21, Vikram noticed that Ankit and Pramod were absent from the factory. Supervisor Shiva Tyagi had also stepped out to drink alcohol. To avoid being detected by the Pitbull dogs, Vikram wrapped himself completely in a tarpaulin sheet. He moved slowly across the factory grounds, freezing whenever the dogs looked in his direction. According to the workers, the dogs mistook him for an abandoned sheet lying on the ground. After reaching the wall, Vikram climbed the Ashoka tree, spread the tarpaulin over the electrified wires to insulate himself and jumped over the boundary. See the spot in 2 pictures, from where the laborer jumped - Crawled five kilometres through sugarcane fields The factory was equipped with CCTV cameras linked directly to Ankit's mobile phone. After escaping, Vikram immediately entered the adjoining sugarcane fields and remained hidden. Soon afterwards, Shiva returned, counted the workers and realised one labourer was missing. He alerted Ankit and Pramod, who arrived and began searching the surrounding fields with torches. Vikram remained concealed throughout the search. Unaware of the location of the nearest police station, he crawled through the sugarcane fields throughout the night, covering nearly five kilometres before reaching Titawi police station at daybreak. There, he informed police that several labourers were being held captive inside the factory. Police raid exposes the horrific conditions Titawi Station House Officer Pramod Kumar immediately informed Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Sanjay Verma. A special team was formed comprising SP (Rural) Akshay Sanjay Mahadik, Circle Officer Vishwajeet Singh, Assistant Labour Commissioner Devesh Singh and Tehsildar Radheshyam Gaur. At around 6 pm on June 22, the team raided the factory. Investigators found 12 labourers confined in one filthy corner of the premises. The Pitbull dogs were well-fed, with meat and bones lying near the entrance. The workers, however, had barely enough food to survive and appeared severely malnourished. Some remained terrified even after police arrived, fearing Ankit or Shiva would return and kill them. Several labourers reportedly asked officers a simple question after being rescued- 'Where are we?' Police arrested Pramod Baliyan and Shiva Tyagi during the raid. Ankit was not found and remains on the run. Police bathed the workers and served them a proper meal The rescued labourers spent the night at the police station. The following morning, police arranged bathing facilities, provided them with clean clothes and prepared a proper meal after learning that many had not eaten decent food for months. Tables and chairs were set up inside the police station, and a local confectioner was called to prepare kheer, poori and potato-chickpea curry. Police personnel personally served the food to the labourers before a court. By then, many of the workers' families had arrived in Muzaffarnagar. Under the Central Government's Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Scheme, each rescued labourer was given a cheque of ₹30,000 before being sent home. Three labourers still missing During questioning, investigators learned that three other labourers who had once worked at the factory were missing. They were identified as Arjun from Nepal, Vishal from Azamgarh and Raju from Sitapur. Police believe that an unidentified body recovered from a canal in Muzaffarnagar in 2025 may be that of Arjun. At the time, the body had been treated as unclaimed. Vishal and Raju remain untraceable. Police have registered a case against Ankit Baliyan, Pramod Baliyan and Shiva Tyagi under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, the Child Labour Act, provisions relating to human trafficking, and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been constituted to investigate the case. Three separate police teams are searching for absconding accused Ankit Baliyan, conducting raids in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Uttarakhand.

stories.title: Pilibhit businessman's murder accused killed in police encounter:₹1.75 lakh bounty holder shot twice in chest, faced 12 criminal cases
stories.summary: The main accused in the murder of businessman Pappu Gupta, Shivam alias Sarvajeet Singh, was killed in a police encounter in Uttar Pradesh's Pilibhit district at around 10 pm on Saturday. A reward of ₹1.75 lakh had been announced for his arrest. Shivam had 12 criminal cases registered against him in Lakhimpur Kheri and neighbouring districts, including two murder cases. Accused opened fire while trying to escape, says SP Pilibhit Superintendent of Police (SP) Sukirti Madhav Mishra said police received information from an informer that Shivam was hiding with one of his associates near Sheetalpur village. When the police team surrounded the area and launched a raid, the accused attempted to flee. His accomplice managed to escape under the cover of darkness. The SP said that, after finding himself surrounded, Shivam opened indiscriminate fire at the police team. Shot during police retaliation, died during treatment According to the SP, the police returned fire in self-defence, during which two bullets in the chest struck Shivam. He was immediately taken to a nearby government hospital. Owing to the seriousness of his injuries, he was referred to a higher medical centre, where he died during treatment. The encounter took place near Sheetalpur village under the jurisdiction of Bilsanda police station. Pappu Gupta was shot while intervening in an argument The incident is linked to the murder of businessman Pappu Gupta on May 28 in the Bilsanda police station area. According to the police, hired the in-laws of businessman Pankaj Katiyar allegedly sent shooters to threaten him. An argument broke out between the armed men and Pankaj outside his shop. Neighbouring businessman Pappu Gupta stepped in to intervene. During the altercation, the assailants opened fire on him, killing him on the spot. Two policemen injured during the encounter SP Sukirti Madhav Mishra said a Special Operations Group (SOG) sub-inspector and a constable sustained bullet injuries during the exchange of fire and have been admitted to hospital. He added that another bullet struck the bulletproof jacket of Bilsanda Station House Officer Jagdeep Malik, preventing what could have been a serious injury.
