stories.title: MBBS student suicide note mentions, 'Don't blame the girl':Was studying at BHU; took an overdose of anaesthesia in hostel
stories.summary: MBBS student Ritvik Kundu (26) committed suicide in Varanasi. At 10 PM on Sunday, Ritvik took an overdose of medicine at Sushrut Hostel of Kashi Hindu University. When senior students called him, there was no response. Concerned, they reached Ritvik's room. When there was no answer to their calls, they contacted the university's Proctorial Office and police. When the door was opened, Ritvik was found lying on the floor. A medicine drip was attached to his hand. When police searched the room, a 3-page suicide note was found. The forensic team also collected evidence. The suicide note read: I was the apple of my family's eye. Perhaps many people like me will not give up in life. But I am giving up. I apologize to all those whose hearts I have hurt. That girl should not be blamed. She is very good. She loved me a lot. She did so much for me. Take care of her. Police say that the initial investigation suggests the cause of death appears to be an overdose of anesthesia medication. The exact cause will be known after the post-mortem. Dr. Ritwik was posted in the anesthesia department. He was studying in MBBS First Year. He was a resident of Hooghly, West Bengal. The incident is from the Lanka police station area. Now understand the entire matter in a sequential manner- What was written in the suicide note? Read Ritvik wrote- Please take care of my parents too. I was their biggest hope. But, I could not live up to their expectations. Life goes on. Perhaps this news will break my mother. She loves me the most. Take care of my father and sister too. I was the apple of their eyes. He wrote, 'As I am writing this, I don't know whether I should change my decision or not. Perhaps I don't want to die, but still I will do this. I am perhaps the most selfish person. Not worthy of living on this earth. It may be that people like me are born only to cause pain to others.' Ritvik wrote- Mother, Father and Sister, please forgive me. I wish I could hear your voice one last time. Everyone, take care of yourselves. Throughout my life, I kept running away from reality. Today I am running away forever. Nothing in this world is permanent. I now understand that I will never be able to live that life. Which I had dreamed of. He said, 'We all dream of a completely happy life. But, perhaps this is not possible for anyone. Life is very short. Don't make it shorter by laughing at others' sorrows. Be kind to everyone and be grateful for what you have. World, goodbye.' Students living in nearby rooms being questioned Lanka Police Station In-charge Rajkumar Verma said - Upon receiving information from the Proctorial Board, the in-charge of Nagwan outpost was sent to the spot. A suicide note was found in the room, the contents of which will be investigated. For now, the body has been taken into custody and kept in the mortuary. The family members have been informed. Students living in nearby rooms have been questioned.

stories.title: Storm and rain in 15 cities of UP, waterlogged underpass:Cars, bikes get stranded; 2 killed in lightning strikes, monsoon likely to enter within 24 hrs
stories.summary: A monsoon-triggering weather system has become active in Uttar Pradesh, paving the way for the arrival of the monsoon in the state. On Monday morning, heavy rainfall was recorded in around 15 cities, including Lucknow, Ayodhya, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Badaun, Maharajganj, Deoria, Kushinagar, and Siddharthnagar. In Mirzapur, so much rain fell that up to 3 feet of water accumulated in an underpass, trapping cars and motorcycles. In Basti and Maharajganj, lightning strikes claimed the lives of a woman and a 9-year-old child. Since morning, most parts of the state have been cloudy, with occasional light sunshine in some areas. An alert has been issued for thunderstorms, rain, and lightning in 46 districts today, while a heatwave warning remains in effect for 26 districts. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the monsoon, stalled near the UP–Bihar border for the past 16 days, may enter Uttar Pradesh within the next 24 hours. According to the IMD, the southwest monsoon will enter the state via eastern Uttar Pradesh. This may lead to intense rainfall in the Terai regions, including Kushinagar, Maharajganj, and Siddharthnagar. Normally, the monsoon arrives in Uttar Pradesh by around June 20, but this year it is running about 9–10 days late. New spell of rain from June 30 Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh from the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said: Due to increased pre-monsoon activity in the state, temperatures have started to drop. The heatwave is now limited to a few cities and is expected to end within 24 hours. After this, a new spell of rainfall will begin in the state from June 30. Conditions are favorable for the southwest monsoon to advance rapidly, which may lead to a temperature drop of 5–7°C in the first week of July. Weather forecast for the next 3 days in UP: June 30: Light rain is expected in western UP, while eastern UP may see heavy rain with thunderstorms. July 1: Western UP will experience rain with thunder, while eastern UP may receive heavy rainfall. July 2: Heavy rain is expected across the entire state, with winds blowing at speeds of 40–50 km/h.

stories.title: Man who charged ₹100 for certificates became 'Bottle Baba':Some followers still believed, even after the arrest, that his 'holy water' cured illnesses
stories.summary: Kanpur's godman 'Bottle Baba' has come under the spotlight after being accused of performing obscene acts while allegedly treating a woman inside a closed room. Despite the allegations, many of his followers continue to stand by him, claiming he could turn ordinary water into "nectar" with a touch and that drinking it cured various ailments. Bottle Baba's real name is Hariom Yadav. Until about a decade ago, he worked at the Kanpur Dehat tehsil, where he processed income and caste certificates. Villagers say he would charge an extra ₹100- ₹150 on top of the official fee for the service. According to locals, Hariom later reappeared dressed in saffron robes, claiming that Goddess Kali had appeared in his dream and instructed him to help devotees and improve their lives. He then built a Kali Mata temple in his village and began calling himself Hari Dham Sarkar. A regular gathering of devotees was held at the temple, where he would blow over water and ask people to drink it, claiming it had healing powers. On June 19, police arrested Hariom Yadav in connection with a molestation case involving a female follower. He is currently in jail, and his ashrams have been shut down. How Hariom became Baba by claiming Kali's command in a dream? Father was a farmer; he himself used to get income-caste certificates made Chain ka Purwa village is about 33 km away from Kanpur Dehat district headquarters. Talking to the people here, it became clear that one section of the village considers Baba a fraud. While many people call him miraculous. According to the villagers, Hariom's father used to do farming. Hariom was not good at studies. He used to help his father with farming at home. After that, he started working on making income-caste certificates at the tehsil of Kanpur Dehat. He used to earn ₹500-₹600 per day. According to villagers, the turning point came in 2015. One day, Hariom gathered people at the village chaupal and claimed that Goddess Kali had appeared in his dream the previous night. He told them she had instructed him to fulfill the purpose for which he was born. Soon after, a new Kali Mata temple was built in the village, where Hariom began conducting religious rituals. He started hearing devotees' grievances and claimed he could solve their problems. Over the next two years, his following grew rapidly, and by 2017, he had become well-known across the surrounding villages. Here, he claimed to cure people in 3 ways- Gradually, people started coming from distant villages. Around the place where Kali Maa's temple is located, Hariom got an ashram built. He started calling the established deity 'Chain Ki Purwa Wali Devi'. He would often have chants of this name raised in his court. Built an ashram on 8 bighas, started holding court here On August 8, 2022, Hariom organized a big event in the village. To inaugurate the ashram, he called Bharat Das Maharaj of Hanumangarhi, Shyam Narayan, President of Jannayak Karpuri Sena, and retired Allahabad High Court Judge Justice Dr. I.M. Qudusi. This ashram was built on the land of the village's Puttilal Yadav. After building the ashram, Hariom started holding court every Tuesday and Saturday. He would sit on a throne in front of people. Sometimes he would wear groom's clothes, and sometimes he would come in dhoti-kurta. Initially, he would issue a receipt for ₹100. One had to buy a water bottle for ₹20 from the ashram shop. Hariom would claim to turn this water into nectar by touching it. If any follower said they didn't benefit, he would say that you are under a shadow. Special worship would need to be performed. People living with Hariom would write down the worship materials, and these had to be purchased from the ashram itself. The cost of materials would be between ₹3 and ₹5 thousand. Village people say that the receipt that cost ₹100 in 2024 has now become ₹250. In the ashram itself, Hariom Yadav's picture was made with the name Haridham Sarkar. It was sold by showing him as God. Often devotees would take these photo frames and put them up in their homes. Bottle Baba claimed to bring the dead back to life These days, a video of Hariom Baba is going viral. In it, he claims to bring a dead woman back to life. He says that I am neither a Baba, nor a devotee, nor any tantric. I have no guru, nor do I wear any kanthi mala (prayer beads). This Sun and this Kali Maa (Goddess Kali), they are my gurus. After this, he starts making gestures with his hands like performing magic. Then the woman lying down gets up, and people start chanting in praise. No one has any information about who this man was. A person associated with Hariom's ashram says that one of Hariom's disciples was from Mumbai. He was in the police. His son suddenly died, after which he went there. When he couldn't bring him back to life, he said that he had reached the feet of God. Now, it won't be right to call him back from there. After this, he returned to his ashram. Apart from Goddess Kali, Hariom would sometimes claim Banke Bihari, Sharda Bhavani, or sometimes Balaji as his guru. He would also make people chant slogans. How did Hariom Yadav finally get caught? On June 5th, Hariom reached a woman's house in Auraiya. Her husband was working in Rajasthan. This house was the woman's maternal home. She had also called her in-laws. After performing the havan-puja, Hariom said that the woman was under the shadow of ghosts and spirits. She would have to come to Haridham Ashram. He asked her to come to the darbar on the new moon day on June 15th. The woman reached the ashram on June 15th with her two brothers-in-law. She says that Hariom took her to a room for exorcism and started molesting her there. After that, I ran outside. Hariom also came out. He said that she is under the shadow of ghosts and spirits; she will have to be whipped. Hariom ordered the woman's brothers-in-law and his nephew to whip her. Everyone kept whipping the woman. She kept pleading with folded hands to be released while crying and writhing in pain. This continued for about 30 minutes. After this, the woman reached Bhognipur police station, about 18 kilometers away from the ashram, and told the police the entire incident. Then the woman's medical examination was conducted. A case was registered against Hariom Yadav, his nephew Deepak, disciple Kundan, and both brothers-in-law Ramvir and Sukhvir. The police arrested Hariom Yadav and his nephew. Hariom says- All the allegations are false. Allegations keep being made against Sanatanists. Ashish Dwivedi, a leader from Dibiyapur, is trying to frame me. I don't have any small ashram, it is built on 8 bighas. After presenting in court, he has been sent to jail.

stories.title: Champat Rai leaves for Delhi three days after resigning:RSS preparing report on Ram Temple donation theft
stories.summary: General Secretary Champat Rai left Ayodhya for Delhi on Sunday evening after resigning from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. He remained at the Ram Temple until around 3 pm before departing. Sources said Champat Rai is likely to attend the Trust meeting scheduled for July 11, where his resignation is expected to be taken up for consideration. He submitted his resignation on Friday. Meanwhile, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is closely monitoring the temple donation theft case. On the instructions of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Eastern Uttar Pradesh regional pracharak Anil Kumar has reached Ayodhya. He has been holding continuous meetings with sadhus, saints, mahants and people associated with the Ram Temple. Sources also said preparations to introduce a new administrative structure in the Ram Temple Trust have gathered pace. A final decision on reconstituting the Trust may be taken after Prime Minister Narendra Modi returns from his overseas visit. Discussions are underway on assigning greater responsibilities to Ayodhya's saints and representatives from various sections of society. The RSS regional pracharak will submit a report to Mohan Bhagwat RSS regional pracharak Anil Kumar, who has been camping in Ayodhya since Saturday (June 27), spent around two hours at the Ram Temple on Saturday evening. He offered prayers to Ram Lalla and also interacted with key temple sevaks. He also held discussions with prominent mahants of Ayodhya regarding the alleged issue of misappropriation of offerings. During these meetings, he spoke with Mahant Maithiliraman Sharan of Lakshman Kila, Dr. Mithileshnandini Sharan of Hanumant Nivas, Mahant Kamalnayan Das, successor of Maniram Das Chhawni, and Mahant Shashikant Das, president of the Saryu Aarti committee, seeking their views. He is expected to continue discussions with saints and mahants in Ayodhya on Monday as well. After completing his interactions, he will compile a detailed report and submit it to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat. Earlier, RSS All India Executive Committee member Bhaiyaji Joshi (Suresh Joshi) had also stayed in Ayodhya for a night and held discussions with saints and mahants associated with the temple. He has already submitted his report to the RSS chief. Ram Mandir's RMO Arjun Dev also on SIT's radar Arjun Dev was responsible for monitoring 1600 cameras A new name has emerged in the investigation of the Ram Temple donation theft case. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has also brought the role of Radio Operation Officer (RMO) Arjun Dev, deployed at Ram Janmabhoomi, under the scope of investigation. Arjun Dev was responsible for monitoring the CCTV cameras installed in the counting room where donations were counted. Besides this, Arjun Dev was also responsible for monitoring approximately 1,600 cameras installed at Ram Janmabhoomi. Now, his role in the surveillance system is being investigated. According to sources, the report also mentions his continuous posting in Ayodhya for 17 years and active interference in the trust's work. RMO Arjun was also handling CCTV work when Ramlalla was in the tent. Arjun Dev appeared arrogantly before SIT The counting of offerings to Ram Lalla in the counting room was monitored by CCTV cameras. The investigating agency is trying to find out how the offerings were stolen despite security arrangements. Why surveillance was not maintained. On this basis, SIT had also questioned Arjun Dev during its initial 3-day investigation. According to sources, when called for questioning, Arjun Dev appeared before the SIT and sat on the chair in a stiff manner. However, instead of answering directly, he said that he would respond through his lawyer. It is being reported that the investigating officers reprimanded him and advised him to maintain the dignity and decorum of his position. Transfer happened many times, but was stopped every time Arjun Dev has been continuously posted in Ayodhya since 2009. During this period, transfer orders were issued several times, but his transfer was stopped every time. Recently, the transfer order issued for Lucknow was also cancelled. Arjun Dev had close relations with some officials of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Due to these connections, his transfers kept getting stopped repeatedly. The SIT is also investigating who was getting the last transfer stopped. Why was the transfer stopped repeatedly? What was the meaning of such a long posting in the same district? Questions also raised on active role in trust's work Apart from CCTV surveillance, Arjun Dev's monitoring also included maintaining wireless communication between police, PAC, CRPF and other security agencies from the control room of the temple premises, staying in contact with personnel on duty, and facilitating immediate exchange of information regarding VIP movement and emergency situations. According to sources, the SIT investigation revealed that Arjun Dev was not limited only to wireless and security-related responsibilities. The investigation has revealed that he also played an active role in several administrative activities of the trust in VIP darshan arrangements. For this reason, questions have also been raised about his working style and activities beyond his jurisdiction. Two years ago, Arjun Dev had stopped the Shankaracharya from darshan About two years ago, Arjun Dev was in the news when he stopped Shankaracharya Swami Vasudevanand Saraswati and his security personnel during the darshan of Ram Lalla. Because the Shankaracharya is associated with the Ram Mandir movement, he wanted to have darshan with his associates and security personnel according to his position and dignity. It is said that citing security reasons, he had allowed only a limited number of people to enter. After this incident, the Shankaracharya returned without darshan in anger. Even at that time, questions were raised about his behavior.

stories.title: NEET student dies by hanging in UP:Writes suicide note to brother on question paper; aspired to become doctor like him
stories.summary: A NEET aspirant in Maharajganj died by suicide after returning home from her examination. She was found hanging at her residence while she was alone at the time of the incident. A suicide note was recovered from the spot, in which she reportedly wrote: “I cannot do anything, my dear brother.” Her family members rushed her to the district hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Following the information, police reached the spot. The student’s doctor brother told officials that the family had never pressured her regarding the exam or studies. He said they had always assured her that whether she got a government medical seat or not, her dream of becoming a doctor would definitely be fulfilled. At the hospital, the brother was seen crying inconsolably while holding his sister’s body. Now the complete incident in detail The incident took place on Monday afternoon in Choupariya Kanchanpur village under the Sadar Kotwali area. The brother, Abhinav Bharati, is a 2021 MBBS batch doctor. The deceased also aspired to become a doctor like him and was preparing for NEET. Abhinav said that his sister had appeared for the NEET exam on May 3, and her paper had not gone well. The family had been continuously reassuring her and motivating her to pursue other medical options like BAMS or private medical colleges if she did not secure a government seat. He added that due to ongoing controversy regarding paper leaks and re-exam discussions, she had been disturbed for the past month and was unable to study properly. Brother says he stepped out for 15 minutes According to the brother, on Sunday she had been checking answers from the exam answer key and became distressed, believing she might not succeed. Under this mental pressure, she took the extreme step. He further said that at the time of the incident, no one was at home. He had stepped out for around 15 minutes, during which the tragedy occurred. The father is a farmer and had fully supported her education and preparation. She was the only sister among two brothers. Her elder brother Abhinav has already cleared NEET in 2021, completed MBBS, and is currently doing internship at Deoria Medical College. Sadar SHO Nirbhay Singh said that the body has been sent for post-mortem. He added that the police are investigating the case from all possible angles, and further action will be taken after the post-mortem report.

stories.title: Tribute paid to deceased students in Lucknow fire:Congress district president demands inspection of coaching centres in Kanpur
stories.summary: Expressing deep sorrow over the untimely deaths of students in the tragic fire incident at a coaching centre in Lucknow, the Kanpur Metropolitan Congress, under the leadership of District President Pawan Gupta, organised a candlelight tribute at Tilak Hall. Under the leadership of District President Pawan Gupta, Congress workers lit candles and paid tribute to the deceased students. They also observed a two-minute silence and prayed for peace to the departed souls. On this occasion, those present expressed their deep condolences to the bereaved families and prayed to God to give them strength to bear this irreparable loss. District President Pawan Gupta said that the incident is extremely tragic and worrying. He stressed that safety standards in educational institutions must be strictly followed so that such painful incidents do not recur in the future. He also said that there are thousands of coaching centres in Kanpur and all of them should be inspected to ensure compliance with safety norms. He demanded a fair investigation into the incident and strict action against those responsible. A large number of Congress office-bearers and workers were present at the condolence meeting and all paid heartfelt tribute to the deceased students. Pawan Gupta, Harprakash Agnihotri, Hamdullah Malik, Ravi Tiwari, Padam Mohan Mishra, Rakesh Sahu, Pramod Gupta, Lallan Awasthi, Dharmendra Singh, Shankar Dutt Mishra, Haji Kausar, Ravi Bajpai, Raju Kashyap, Vinod Awasthi, Rajendra Valmiki, Mohammad Aftab, Brijesh Gupta and others were present.

stories.title: ₹11 crore gold purchase used to launder fraud money:Mumbai Crime Branch raids continue in Gorakhpur, hunt on for 2 suspects
stories.summary: A cyber fraud case that has shocked investigators has come to light in Gorakhpur, where a Mumbai-based gang allegedly used proceeds of fraud to purchase jewellery worth around ₹11 crore from multiple showrooms across the city. The accused first transferred money through online advance payments and then sent their associates to collect the jewellery. Since the payments were credited to the bank accounts of the jewellers on time, no suspicion was raised. A team from the Mumbai Crime Branch’s cyber cell is currently conducting raids and investigations in Gorakhpur, Deoria and Kushinagar. Searches are also underway for two suspected individuals linked to the case. Fraud routed through mule accounts According to information, cyber criminals did not use the fraud money directly. Instead, it was first routed through mule bank accounts. From these accounts, payments were then made to the bank accounts of well-known jewellery showrooms in Gorakhpur. As soon as the money reflected in the shopkeepers’ accounts, members of the gang would visit the stores and collect gold ornaments. Sources say this entire racket has been running for the past three months, with most purchases made from jewellery showrooms in the Civil Lines and Asuran areas of the city. Advance bookings used for delivery The fraudsters were highly organised. In several cases, they made advance online payments first and then sent their men the next day to pick up the jewellery. Since the payments were credited on time, shopkeepers did not suspect any wrongdoing. Mumbai Cyber Cell officials have so far visited at least four major jewellery showrooms in the city. Investigators are examining sale bills, documents and CCTV footage to identify the individuals who collected the jewellery and trace the wider network. Local youths allegedly hired on commission Investigating agencies suspect that the gang recruited several local youths in Gorakhpur and nearby areas by offering commissions. During the probe, the names of two suspects from Gopalganj (Bihar) and Deoria have surfaced. Police are now examining their bank accounts, mobile numbers and financial transactions to uncover the full network.

stories.title: 'Dad, there is fire, I am in bathroom, save me':Mother cries, pleads 'find my child', then faints; heart-wrenching stories of Lucknow fire tragedy
stories.summary: Dad, please save me. I won’t survive now. The fire has spread across the entire building. We have locked ourselves inside the bathroom. Smoke is also entering here. I am struggling to breathe,” the student said while crying on the phone. The father of the trapped student reached the spot immediately after receiving the call. He kept searching for his son in panic, showing his photograph to people and asking if anyone had seen him. Meanwhile, a mother who had reached the site fainted while pleading with others to help find her son. The building also housed a pet shop. Several pets, including dogs and cats, were trapped in the fire. As soon as a woman learned that her pets were inside, she broke down in tears. Parents of trapped students kept appealing to Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak and officials with folded hands, requesting them to rescue their children. Father said - As soon as I got my son's call, I ran towards the coaching center Prabhujyoti Singh said his son made the distress call from inside the coaching centre. “My son Sukhmani Singh called me and said there is a fire, please save us. Then the call got disconnected. I immediately rushed here. On the way, I kept calling ambulances and the fire brigade, but I could not get through for a long time,” he said. He added that he has not been able to speak to his son again since then. His phone is switched off. While saying this, Prabhujyoti Singh broke down in tears. Mother said - Someone please find my child... Another student, Aditya Srivastava, was also reported missing after the incident. There was no information about him. He had reportedly called a friend saying he was trapped and needed help, after which he went out of contact. His friend informed his mother, who rushed to the site crying and asking everyone about her son. She kept pleading, “Someone please find my son… what will we do now?” Overcome with grief, she fainted on the spot. People present there helped her recover. Later, it was confirmed that Aditya Srivastava had died in the incident. Locked themselves in washroom to escape from fire Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak reached the site and spoke to students who were inside the building during the fire. They informed him that 3–4 students had locked themselves inside a bathroom to escape the flames. Fire brigade teams reached the upper floors and checked each room and bathroom one by one during the rescue operation. Coaching employee said- I climbed down holding the wire A coaching centre employee, Mohammad Asin, said that as soon as they got information about the fire, they ran outside. Smoke had filled the staircases and rooms. “I came down from the upper floor by holding onto a wire. Only then could I save myself,” he said. He added that initially he thought it was a small fire, but it quickly turned massive. Realising the danger, he escaped by climbing down using a wire. Woman kept crying to save her stomach A woman who reached the spot with her family said two of her pets were inside the pet shop in the building. When she could not get any information about them, she began crying uncontrollably and appealed to officials to save them as well.

stories.title: 15 dead in fire at Lucknow coaching centre:AC short circuit suspected as cause; 4 officers suspended, 3 accused arrested
stories.summary: A devastating fire tore through a building in Lucknow on Monday afternoon, claiming 15 lives. Most of the victims were students in their 20s and 30s attending a coaching centre on the second floor. The casualties include 10 men and 5 women. According to reports, after the fire spread, students locked themselves in the bathroom. One child jumped from the first floor to save his life, but fell onto the grill below and was seriously injured. CM Yogi has suspended four officers. An FIR has been filed against three of the accused and they have been arrested. Building housed a pet shop, coaching centre and game studio The building where the fire broke out is located in the Aliganj area. The basement, ground, and first floors house a pet shop and a clinic. The second floor houses a library called Learning Space (used as a coaching centre) and Head Hopper Studio, which handles 3D art production and game asset outsourcing. Short circuit suspected as cause The cause of the fire is suspected that it was caused by a short circuit in the AC system in the basement. Around 10 fire brigade vehicles are at the scene. The SDRF and NDRF have also arrived. Firefighters have broken down the rear wall of the building and are recovering bodies. Ambulances were insufficient to transport the dead and injured. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak, who was present at the scene, wept at the sight. He said, “I saw bodies being carried before my eyes.” PM announces ₹2 lakh relief Meanwhile, PM Modi announced that an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each deceased. The injured would be given Rs 50,000. Visuals from the incident: Location of the incident: Follow our live blog for regular updates…

stories.title: Wrestler sets herself on fire at Bijnor police station:Had earlier filed rape a case against a soldier; condition serious
stories.summary: A female wrestler set herself on fire at Kotwali city police station in Bijnor on Sunday night, protesting police inaction in an alleged rape case she had filed against a soldier. The incident occurred at 10:45 pm. As soon as the female wrestler was on fire, she started screaming and ran in the station. During this, the fire spread onto the curtains of the inspector's chamber. Police personnel present at the scene extinguished the fire and took the woman to the district hospital. Doctors administered primary treatment and referred her to a hospital in Meerut. Currently, the woman's condition is critical. Doctors said she has suffered 60 per cent burns. The police's initial investigation revealed that the female wrestler had a love affair with a soldier. It is alleged that the soldier had promised marriage but later backed out. Following this, the woman had filed an FIR against him for rape. The accused soldier had obtained a stay on his arrest from court, due to which the police were unable to take action against him. Angered by this, the woman took the extreme step. In this matter, SP Abhishek Jha has suspended station in-charge sub-inspector Amar Singh Rathore with immediate effect. Sequence of events The woman is 25 years old. She has studied M.Sc and also wrestles. Her father was a home guard. He died in a shooting incident at the DM's residence a long time ago. After this, her mother remarried. The woman has a brother. It is being said that three years ago, the female wrestler met Saurabh, a soldier from Bijnor, at Saraswati Vidya Mandir. After this, the two became very close. Saurabh had promised to marry the female wrestler, but later backed out. SP Abhishek Jha stated that the young woman had previously filed a rape case against Saurabh. Due to lack of evidence, the police had filed a final report in the case. After this, the young woman again filed a report against the young man, on which the police had filed a charge sheet in court. Saurabh had obtained a stay on his arrest from the High Court. Came to the police station in the afternoon, set herself on fire at night The female wrestler came to the city police station with her mother on Sunday afternoon. She demanded action against Saurabh. Police personnel explained to her the developments in the case and asked her to return home. After this, she again reached the police station on Sunday night and started demanding the arrest of the soldier. When the police personnel did not listen to her, she poured petrol and set herself on fire. Upon receiving information about the incident, there was a stir in the police department. SP Abhishek Jha and SP City Dr. Krishna Gopal Singh immediately reached the police station. SP Abhishek Jha said- The woman is about 60% burnt. Currently, she is undergoing treatment in Meerut. Upon checking CCTV footage, it was found that her stepfather Naresh had given the woman the bottle of oil.

stories.title: Fake tea tip-off uncovers major counterfeit goods racket:Counterfeit packing of Harpic, Fair Lovely and Eno seized in Gorakhpur; case registered
stories.summary: A major counterfeit goods racket has been uncovered in Gorakhpur during a raid linked to the fake packaging of Brookbond Taaza tea. During the operation, officials recovered not only counterfeit tea products but also suspicious packaging of several well-known brands, including Fair Lovely face cream, Harpic and Eno. The Food Safety Department has sealed the entire stock. Based on a complaint filed by a company representative, a case has been registered against shop owner Abhishek Kumar Gupta under the Copyright Act at Cantt Police Station. Officials posed as customers to trace the store The Food Safety Department had received information that counterfeit products of reputed companies were being sold in the city. However, officials were initially unable to identify the exact location of the store. To track it down, the team contacted the supplier while posing as customers and placed an order for tea leaves. Around six hours later, the delivery arrived at the designated address. Officials then accompanied the delivery person to a store in Bilandpur, where they discovered a large stockpile of suspected counterfeit goods. Counterfeit products found across multiple brands During the inspection, officials recovered suspicious packaging and products linked to several brands, including Brookbond Tea, Everest Masala, Cadbury Gems and Rajesh Masala. The seized items included- Samples of all recovered products have been sent for laboratory examination. Case registered following company complaint A case has been lodged at Cantt Police Station on the complaint of Amit Kumar Mall, Senior Investigator Officer at Check IP Solution Private Limited, Lucknow. Police and the Food Safety Department are jointly investigating the matter. Store operated quietly in residential area Company representatives had informed authorities that Brookbond Taaza tea was being sold in fake packaging in the Cantt area. Despite several attempts, officials were unable to locate the premises. After obtaining the supplier's mobile number, the department placed an order on Saturday morning. When the delivery arrived at around 6 pm, officials followed the delivery route and reached the store. Investigators were surprised to find suspected counterfeit products of several other companies alongside the fake tea packaging. Source of counterfeit packaging under investigation During questioning, the shop owner claimed he sourced the goods from Maharajganj. However, officials are not fully convinced by his statement. Investigators suspect the counterfeit packaging may have been manufactured elsewhere and supplied through the Gorakhpur outlet. Efforts are now underway to identify the wider network and locate the packaging unit involved. Crackdown on counterfeit goods to continue Food Safety Department officials said some traders are exploiting the names of established brands to sell fake products. They noted that previous raids in the Kotwali area had also led to the recovery of counterfeit packaging for products such as Tata Salt, tea leaves and Fevikwik. Authorities said their campaign against adulteration and the sale of counterfeit products will continue.

stories.title: 200-year-old Tazia brought out in Varanasi:Historic Mughal-Iranian design structure taken out for Muharram observances
stories.summary: The Tazia of Mote Shaban at the Baradari Imambara in Doshipura, Varanasi, was brought out from the Baradari Mosque and installed on the occasion of 6th Muharram (Monday). The 200-year-old Tazia has been taken out annually since 1981 after the seals on eight locks are opened in the presence of police and administrative officials. Hundreds of devotees gathered inside and outside the mosque during the process. The Tazia, which is stored in separate sections throughout the year, was carefully brought out piece by piece from the chamber (hujra) where it is kept. See pictures- History of the Tazia 200-year-old structure carried by 60 people Gulzar Ali said the Tazia is popularly known as the Tazia of his ancestor, Mote Shaban, who died in 1857. The structure predates his lifetime and was already being carried in religious observances before then. Mote Shaban was closely associated with the then Kashi Naresh, and since his era, the Tazia has been brought out from the mosque and installed at the Baradari every year on 6th Muharram. The Tazia is carried by around 60 people and consists of 22 individual sections, including five principal components. Among them is the main dome, which features silver and gold ornamentation. The structure is crafted from teak wood and decorated with intricate Mughal and Iranian-style designs.

stories.title: 70-foot slab of under-construction bridge collapses in Hardoi:Slipped while being lifted by crane, 2 labourers gets trapped
stories.summary: A 70-foot concrete slab of an under-construction bridge over the Sharda Canal in Hardoi collapsed on Monday morning, trapping two labourers beneath the debris. Both workers sustained serious injuries in the accident. The incident occurred while a crane was lifting the massive slab into position on the bridge under construction. Following the collapse, rescue teams used a crane and bulldozer to remove the fallen slab and free the trapped workers. The injured labourers, identified as Rahul (30) and Gendalal (35), both residents of Sidhauli, were rushed to the district hospital. After receiving primary treatment, they were referred to a medical college due to the severity of their injuries. DM orders investigation Hardoi District Magistrate Anunay Jha has ordered an inquiry into the incident. He said strict action would be taken against those found responsible once the investigation is completed. The bridge is being constructed by RCL Company as part of the Lucknow–Palia National Highway project. Residents claimed that a section of the same under-construction bridge had also collapsed around 1.5 months ago. Part of ₹600-crore highway project According to NHAI Assistant Engineer Pushpesh Yadav, the bridge forms part of a ₹600-crore highway project stretching from Shahabad to Khetui village in Hardoi district. An overbridge is currently being built near Saidpur village in the Behta Gokul police station area. Construction began in November 2023 and was scheduled for completion by November 2025. However, delays in shifting high-tension power lines have slowed progress. See 4 pictures related to the accident-

stories.title: 21-year-old SP office demolished in Sitapur:Bulldozer action begins at 4 AM; lease was granted during Mulayam's government
stories.summary: A Samajwadi Party (SP) office built on government land in Sitapur, UP, was demolished early on Monday morning. The district administration reached the spot at 4 am with forces from 5 police stations. Four bulldozers razed the office to the ground in 2 hours. The debris was also removed. During this, 25 policemen and 50 Pradeshik Armed Constabulary jawans remained deployed. Sadar SDM Dr. Janardan Kumar and several other officials were also present. The SP office was built 21 years ago on 2,500 square feet of land. The lease was given in the name of the SP office on government Nazul land. However, the lease was cancelled four months later. At that time, Mulayam Singh Yadav was the Chief Minister. Even after the lease was cancelled, the SP office continued to operate here. Fifteen days ago, the district magistrate's court had sent a notice to SP district president Chhatrapal Yadav. He was given time till Sunday to vacate the office. The SP district president had vacated the office 24 hours before the bulldozer action. Pictures of the bulldozer action- Sequence of events Seema Singh, the executive officer (EO) of the Municipal Council, said, "On January 15, 2005, the then Municipal Council president Radheshyam Jaiswal had allotted the Nazul land of the Town Hall complex for the SP district office. The rent for this was fixed at only ₹100.' She said, “A hall and two rooms were built on 2,500 square feet of land. However, within a few months, the allotment came under dispute. During the investigation, irregularities in the observance of rules and legal provisions in the allotment process came to light. The Municipal Council had cancelled the allotment on April 14, 2005.” SP MP says the BJP will have to bear the loss for this Anand Bhadauria, SP MP from Dhaurahra, said, “Legally, our side was weak in the office matter, but the way BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party) demolished the office by deploying bulldozers early in the morning, Samajwadi supporters will never forget it. The public will surely break BJP's arrogance. BJP will have to pay the price for this.” BJP district president says action against breaking of rules Rajesh Shukla, BJP district president of Sitapur, said the BJP government works in accordance to the law. “The administration will take action against anyone who violates the rules,” he said.

stories.title: 'Saifai family took money in Gomti Riverfront scam':Minister Rajbhar says, 'I am sitting with complete file, will reveal all secrets one by one'
stories.summary: Raising the political temperature in Uttar Pradesh, Om Prakash Rajbhar, chief of the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) and a cabinet minister in the Yogi government, once again launched a sharp attack on Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Monday. Rajbhar accused Akhilesh of diverting funds allocated for the Gomti Riverfront Project to finance the 2017 Assembly elections. He claimed that after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's demonetisation move, Akhilesh could no longer rely on the alleged black money of gangster-politician Atiq Ahmed, prompting him to use project funds instead. The minister also said he would expose alleged corruption during the SP regime "one file at a time". Read what allegations Minister Rajbhar made against Akhilesh Yadav... 'Entire budget spent, only 60% of work completed' Rajbhar alleged that despite the entire project budget being spent, only 60 per cent of the Gomti Riverfront Project was completed. According to him, funds meant for the remaining 40 per cent of the work ended up in the coffers of the "Saifai family" and were used during the Assembly elections. Taking a swipe at Akhilesh Yadav, Rajbhar said the former chief minister believed his alleged wrongdoing would remain hidden after returning to power, but "the cup of sin had overflowed". He added that the government of "scammers" lost power and the alleged irregularities subsequently came to light. 'No air Conditioning in jail, no press conferences either' Rajbhar described the Gomti Riverfront case as only one example of what he called corruption during the SP government. He claimed to possess several files related to alleged irregularities and said each case would be revealed in due course. He also stated that investigating agencies are probing the Riverfront Project and that the truth would soon emerge. In a sarcastic remark aimed at Akhilesh Yadav, Rajbhar said: Have patience. In jail, you will get neither air conditioning nor access to Twitter, and you will not be able to hold press conferences. What is the Gomti Riverfront project case? The Samajwadi Party government sanctioned ₹1,513 crore for the Gomti Riverfront Project. According to official records, ₹1,437 crore was released, yet only around 60 per cent of the work was completed. Despite nearly 95 per cent of the budget being disbursed, about 40 per cent of the project remained unfinished. Allegations were later made that tender conditions had been altered to favour a defaulting company. Around 800 tenders were reportedly issued for the project, with authority vested in the Chief Engineer. Yogi government ordered judicial probe After coming to power, the Yogi Adityanath government constituted an inquiry committee headed by retired High Court judge Justice Alok Singh to investigate the alleged scam. Based on the committee's findings, further action was initiated. In December 2017, the CBI registered an FIR in connection with the Riverfront Project. The FIR named eight individuals, including- Of the eight individuals named in the FIR, seven have since retired from government service. Cases were registered under provisions related to financial irregularities and alleged corruption. In July 2017, the Uttar Pradesh government formally recommended a CBI investigation. Along with the recommendation, it submitted the judicial inquiry report, a copy of the FIR registered at Gomtinagar police station and other relevant documents. Rajbhar repeats claim of imminent split in SP During the ongoing monsoon session, Rajbhar once again claimed that the Samajwadi Party is heading towards an internal split. Referring to the splits in the Trinamool Congress in West Bengal and the Shiv Sena in Maharashtra, he said the next political break-up would occur in Uttar Pradesh. Rajbhar claimed that a division within the SP would emerge during the monsoon session and would be led by what he described as the "rebel son of Ballia". He further alleged that Ram Gopal Yadav had submitted a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Rajbhar also claimed that Ram Gopal Yadav's son, Shivpal Yadav, his son, and several other family members were linked to the Gomti Riverfront case. Referring to Akhilesh Yadav's recent remarks that the BJP had poached SP legislators, Rajbhar said- Those who are weak and timid will leave. Apart from four or five family members, everyone is prepared to abandon him. SP leaders reject Rajbhar's claims Rajbhar's assertions have been dismissed by several Samajwadi Party leaders. More than 20 party MPs, including Ballia MP Sanatan Pandey, rejected the claim that the SP was facing a split. Even Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya described Rajbhar's prediction as baseless. Amid the war of words, a hoarding targeting Rajbhar appeared outside the Samajwadi Party headquarters in Lucknow. The hoarding was put up by SP leader Mohammad Ikhlaq Ahmed, who mocked Rajbhar's claims. Alongside Rajbhar's photograph, the message read- My own MLAs are roaming around carrying the SP flag, and I am talking about breaking the party. What answer will I give when the public asks questions? Ikhlaq Ahmed said that Rajbhar, Minister Sanjay Nishad, and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya have repeatedly claimed that the Samajwadi Party is on the verge of a split. He countered that Rajbhar's own MLAs openly identify with the Samajwadi Party and regard Akhilesh Yadav as their leader. Ahmed also targeted Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad, saying he entered mainstream politics and became an MP with the support of Akhilesh Yadav before later joining the ruling alliance.

stories.title: ₹12-crore Ayodhya cruise standing from 3-months:Tourist numbers fall after fares double; Boatmen offer rides for ₹50
stories.summary: While the alleged theft of offerings at Ayodhya's Ram Mandir remains under investigation, another project has come under scrutiny, the Water Metro introduced on the Saryu River. The vessel, brought from Kochi at a cost of around ₹12 crore, has remained stationary for the past three months. The Water Metro was originally intended to operate along a 14-kilometre route between Ram Ghat and Guptar Ghat. However, citing fluctuating water levels, too low at times and excessively high at others, authorities restricted operations to a two-kilometre stretch near Tulsi Ghat (Naya Ghat). Services have now been completely suspended. Questions are being raised over whether the Water Metro will resume operations and whether it will ever operate on its originally planned route. Private operator took over, fare doubled During a visit to Ayodhya, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Sudhakar, an employee associated with the Water Metro project. He said the original route had been finalised before operations began, but the vessel's height created an unforeseen obstacle. According to him, the Water Metro cannot pass beneath the bridge connecting Ayodhya and Gonda. As a result, instead of travelling to Guptar Ghat as planned, it was confined to operating around Tulsi Ghat. Asked whether the Water Metro could eventually reach Guptar Ghat, Sudhakar pointed to another challenge, heavy siltation in the Saryu River. He said that even after dredging, silt quickly accumulates again. During the monsoon, rising water levels further reduce the clearance beneath the bridge, making regular services to Guptar Ghat difficult. Sudhakar also attributed declining passenger numbers to a sharp fare increase. According to him, until 2025, the service was operated by the tourism department and charged ₹150 per passenger. Passenger numbers were reasonable at that rate. However, after operations were handed over to JS Cleantech Private Limited, the fare was increased to ₹300, leading to a decline in ridership. Boatmen claim electricity dues remain unpaid Local boat operators told Bhaskar that most visitors to Ayodhya return after visiting the Ram Mandir, while those who do reach the riverfront generally opt for cheaper alternatives. The Water Metro charges ₹300 per ride, whereas traditional boat operators offer trips for between ₹50 and ₹100. Some boatmen also claimed that the Water Metro project has accumulated an outstanding electricity bill of ₹21–22 lakh, which they say is one reason the vessel remains idle. The operating company has not confirmed this claim. Boatman Jitendra Manjhi said he returned to Ayodhya from Mumbai after the Ram Mandir was built, expecting better business opportunities. Initially, earnings were strong, but the growing number of boats operating on the river has reduced income significantly. He said there are days when he is left with savings of only ₹400–500 after a full day's work. Revenue too low to sustain operations Vivek Rai, the Water Metro manager, said that when UP Tourism operated the service, passengers paid ₹150 for a ride lasting around 25 minutes. Under the current arrangement, passengers pay ₹300 for a journey lasting approximately 40 to 45 minutes. When asked about the future of the service, Rai said the decision does not rest with the local operational team. According to him, his team is responsible only for maintenance and day-to-day operations, while decisions regarding the project's future will be taken by higher authorities. Another individual associated with the project said the vessel has a capacity of around 50 passengers, but even during operations, it was difficult to attract more than 10 to 15 passengers per trip. He added that revenue was insufficient even to cover the salaries of the project's 10 employees. While he acknowledged that electricity dues were pending, he said he could not confirm the exact amount owed. Questions raised over planning and route selection The Water Metro was launched with the aim of boosting tourism and river transport in Ayodhya. However, the project has yet to achieve the success envisioned by planners. Questions are now being raised about the initial survey, route selection and feasibility assessment. The Saryu River experiences significant fluctuations in water levels throughout the year. Water levels often fall sharply during dry periods, while monsoon rains can cause the river to swell considerably. Silt accumulation is another persistent issue. Even after dredging channels for navigation, sediment quickly builds up again, affecting operations. Critics argue that despite these known challenges, infrastructure, including jetties, charging stations and related facilities, was developed without adequately addressing the river's operational constraints. As planning concerns continue to grow, discussions have now emerged about constructing a barrage on the Saryu River in an effort to facilitate regular Water Metro operations in Ayodhya.

stories.title: NEET re-exam exposes solver gang in Bihar, 24 arrested:PMCH students allegedly agreed to write exam for ₹30-40 lakh; biometric company staff also held
stories.summary: The NEET-UG 2026 re-examination, conducted on Sunday after the 3 May paper leak, led to the exposure of a major solver gang in Bihar's Lakhisarai district. Police investigations revealed that medical students allegedly agreed to appear in the examination on behalf of candidates for Rs 30-40 lakh. Police have arrested 24 people in the case, including the alleged gang leader, medical students and employees of a biometric verification company. The arrested students are from PMCH, Gaya Medical College, AIIMS Raebareli and BHU. Fourteen employees of the biometric verification company have also been taken into custody. Raids were conducted at Rajkiya High School Hasanpur, KRK Higher Secondary School and Kendriya Vidyalaya examination centres. According to Lakhisarai SP Prerna, mobile phones and important documents were recovered from the accused. CBI had questioned alleged kingpin in 2024 Arpit Raj, identified by police as the alleged kingpin of the solver gang, had earlier come under the scanner in NEET-related investigations. During the probe into the 2024 NEET paper leak case, the CBI questioned him several times. Nine suspected solvers detained Police and district authorities detained nine suspected "Munna Bhais" after receiving information about solver gang activity during the re-examination. According to sources, one suspect was caught at the KRK School examination centre, seven at Kendriya Vidyalaya and one at Hasanpur School. All are reportedly residents of Lakhisarai district. PMCH student entered centre posing as employee Investigators found that Mayank Kashyap, a PMCH student from Hajipur, allegedly entered the Hasanpur examination centre by posing as an employee of the biometric verification company. Police arrested him at the centre. His interrogation led investigators to other biometric company employees, helping police uncover the wider network. Health department's monitoring comes under scrutiny To prevent medical students from acting as solvers, the Health Department organised department-wise seminars and quizzes from 2 pm to 5 pm on Sunday at PMCH and other medical colleges across Bihar. Attendance was made compulsory for students. Despite these measures, the arrest of a third-year PMCH student in the case has raised questions about the department's monitoring system and security arrangements. Physics paper toughest, Biology easier The NEET-UG 2026 re-examination was conducted at around 5,400 centres across the country. Students reported mixed reactions after the exam. Experts said the paper focused more on conceptual understanding and clarity than rote learning. Physics was considered the most difficult and lengthy section, while Chemistry remained moderate, with many questions directly based on NCERT. Biology was relatively easier. According to experts, the difficult Physics section could reduce average scores by 10-20 marks and may lower the overall cut-off by 10-15 marks. Question papers reached Bihar on 16 June The question papers for the re-examination arrived at Patna Airport on 16 June aboard a special Indian Air Force aircraft. From there, they were distributed to examination authorities in Patna, Darbhanga, Gaya and other locations. The re-examination was conducted on 22 June after the earlier NEET-UG exam was cancelled following the paper leak controversy.

stories.title: UP STF guns down Bihar Gangster Lalan Singh:Accused in seven murders; 2 brothers were also killed in earlier police encounters
stories.summary: Bihar's notorious criminal Lalan Singh alias Lallan was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) in Saharanpur during the early hours of Monday. Lalan was wanted in several serious criminal cases across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, including the murders of seven people, among them two sub-inspectors, a bank cashier and a security guard, as well as robbery, ATM cash van lootings and other violent offences. A total reward of ₹1.25 lakh had been announced for information leading to his arrest. STF team came under fire during vehicle check According to ADG Amitabh Yash, a UP STF team led by ASP Lal Pratap Singh was conducting a checking operation on the Sarsawa–Nakud Road at around 1.30 am on Sunday night. During the operation, officers spotted suspicious men approaching on a motorcycle. When they were asked to stop, the suspects allegedly opened fire on the STF team. The STF retaliated, during which Lalan Singh was shot and fell to the ground. His accomplice managed to escape under the cover of darkness. The injured Lalan was initially taken to a Community Health Centre (CHC) and later referred to the district hospital due to his critical condition, where doctors declared him dead. The encounter took place within the Sarsawa police station area. Brothers also killed in earlier police encounter Police said Lalan's brothers, Rajnish alias Baua Singh and Manish Singh, were killed in a police encounter four years ago. Lalan escaped during that operation and had been absconding ever since. Investigators say the three brothers were involved in numerous high-profile crimes across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. See pictures- Family background According to police records, Lalan was a resident of Nandgolwa village in the Mohiuddin Nagar police station area of Samastipur district, Bihar. His father, Shiv Shankar Singh, is a farmer. The family comprises five sons and three daughters. Police claim that four of the brothers, Lalan, Rajneesh, Manish and Babua Singh, became involved in criminal activities and operated as a gang. Of the four- Lalan, Rajneesh and Manish have been killed in police encounters. Babua Singh is currently lodged in Hajipur Jail. The eldest brother, Pattharu Singh, works in the private sector and has no criminal record. Brother Failed SBI PO Selection Before Turning to Crime According to sources, Rajneesh Singh had cleared the written examination for the State Bank of India Probationary Officer (PO) recruitment process in 2016 but did not make the final merit list. Following this setback, he allegedly turned to crime and later formed a gang with his brothers Manish and Lalan. The trio subsequently became wanted by police forces in both Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Reward announced after murder and robbery cases Police said Lalan, Rajneesh and Manish were involved in the shooting of a sub-inspector in Varanasi and the theft of his government-issued pistol. On 1 November 2022, the trio allegedly murdered a young man in Chandauli and stole his motorcycle. Following these incidents, a reward of ₹1 lakh was announced for Lalan in Varanasi and ₹25,000 in Chandauli. Sub-inspector shot in Varanasi On the evening of 8 November 2022, Lalan and his brothers allegedly shot Sub-Inspector Ajay Yadav, a 2015-batch officer posted at Luxa Police Station, in the chest. Ajay Yadav, a resident of Bhikhampur village in Pratapgarh, was attacked before the accused fled with his government pistol, ten cartridges, purse and mobile phone. Despite being seriously injured, the officer reportedly ran to a hospital on foot. Doctors performed emergency surgery, removed the bullet and saved his life. Twelve days later, on 21 November 2022, Varanasi Police tracked down the three brothers on the Ring Road in the Baragaon police station area. During the encounter, Rajneesh and Manish were killed, while Lalan escaped. Their father reportedly refused to accept their bodies, stating that he no longer had any connection with them. The police later performed their last rites at Harishchandra Ghat. Escape from Patna Court and hideout in Varanasi The three brothers were also accused in a major daylight robbery at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch near Baghatilha village in Bihar's Belchhi police station area on 6 March 2017. During the robbery, security guards Yogeshwar Paswan, Suresh Singh, and driver Ajit Yadav were shot dead, and around ₹60 lakh was looted. On 9 September 2022, the brothers escaped from custody by breaking through a toilet wall at the Barh District Court in Patna. After fleeing, they reportedly went into hiding in the Manduadih area of Varanasi. Criminal record of Lalan Singh 16 March 2016- ASI Bhuvaneshwar Singh shot and injured in Nalanda, Bihar. Government revolver looted. 18 April 2016- ASI Suresh Thakur was murdered in Patna. The government pistol was looted. 24 September 2016- ASI R.R. Chaudhary was murdered in Patna. The government pistol was looted. 27 February 2017- Two people were murdered during a cash van robbery in Nalanda; around ₹20 lakh was looted. 6 March 2017- Personnel transporting bank cash were attacked in Patna. Three people murdered and approximately ₹60 lakh was looted. 29 March 2017- Case registered in Patna for attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms. 8 September 2022- Case registered in Patna for escape from custody and assisting others to escape. 30 October 2022- Theft case registered in Lanka, Varanasi. 1 November 2022- Lalbabu Chauhan shot dead and a Pulsar motorcycle looted in Chandauli's Sakaldiha area. 8 November 2022- Sub-Inspector Ajay Yadav shot in Varanasi, his government pistol and other belongings looted. 21 November 2022- Fired upon a police team during an encounter in the Dabhan area of Varanasi. The looted government pistol was recovered. April–May 2023- Cases registered in Rohania and Dabhan police stations, Varanasi, for failing to comply with court proclamation proceedings.

stories.title: Rain in 5 UP districts, heatwave alert in 38:Temperature crosses 42°C; severe heat expected for next 3 days
stories.summary: The delay in the arrival of the monsoon has intensified heat across Uttar Pradesh, with temperatures crossing 42°C in several districts. Most cities witnessed strong sunshine from Monday morning onwards. Combined with cloud movement and slow wind speeds, humidity levels have also increased significantly. The Meteorological Department has issued a heatwave alert for 38 districts, while a rain warning has been issued for Mau, Chandauli, Ballia, Ghazipur and Sonbhadra. Monsoon stalled near UP-Bihar border According to the Meteorological Department, the monsoon usually enters Uttar Pradesh by 20 June. This year, however, it has been unable to advance after reaching the UP-Bihar border. For the past 10 to 12 days, the monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj. Meteorologists expect it to begin advancing again from 23 June and enter Uttar Pradesh around 25 June. Until then, residents of Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bundelkhand are likely to continue facing intense heat and heatwave conditions. Prayagraj and Varanasi among hottest cities Over the past 24 hours, most districts recorded strong sunshine. Ghaziabad and Bareilly remained cloudy, while Lucknow and surrounding areas experienced hot winds throughout the day. The highest temperatures recorded in the state were- Prayagraj: 42.5°C Varanasi: 42.4°C Bahraich: 42°C Jhansi: 41.8°C Rainfall Recorded in Several Districts While most of the state remained dry, some districts received light rainfall. Kheragarh (Agra)- 18 mm Govardhan (Mathura)- 5 mm Mau- 4 mm Chark (Sonbhadra)- 8.6 mm Sultanpur- 8.6 mm Heatwave conditions likely to intensify Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said that Uttar Pradesh is likely to experience severe heat for the next three days. According to him, temperatures will continue to rise and heatwave conditions are expected to become more intense. He added that the monsoon's progress remains slow and favourable conditions for its entry into the state have not yet developed. Residents may have to wait at least three to four more days for the arrival of the monsoon. 5-day weather forecast for Uttar Pradesh 23 June- Weather is expected to remain clear across both Eastern and Western Uttar Pradesh. Strong sunshine and hot winds are likely. No significant rainfall is expected. 24 June- Cloud cover is expected over most districts. Heavy rainfall may occur at isolated locations in Eastern Uttar Pradesh, while Western Uttar Pradesh is likely to remain largely clear. 25 June- Rainfall activity may increase in Eastern Uttar Pradesh, accompanied by strong winds. The monsoon may also enter the state around this time. Heatwave conditions are expected to persist in Western Uttar Pradesh. 26 June- Cloudy conditions are likely across the state. Rain accompanied by strong winds may occur in several districts, bringing some relief from the heat. 27 June- Heavy rainfall is possible in both Eastern and Western Uttar Pradesh. Temperatures may fall below 40°C, providing significant respite from the ongoing heatwave.

stories.title: Ram Mandir theft case:FIR likely within 2 days; 80 people, including Tinnu Yadav may be named, SIT to submit report to Yogi today
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating the theft of offerings at Ram Mandir may submit its preliminary report to CM Yogi today. The team had reached to meet Yogi on Sunday evening, but the meeting could not take place. The CM was busy with the monsoon session and other meetings. The SIT has saved data in 7 pen drives. In the 6-day investigation, names of 150 suspects have emerged. Action may be taken against 25 of them. Those whom the SIT has already questioned have been warned not to go anywhere outside until further orders. These include Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Anil Mishra. The SIT may also file an FIR in the case today or tomorrow. 80 people including Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu and Anukalp, who are close to Champat Rai, may be named. Names of Trust officials are also being mentioned in this. Tinnu is close to Champat Rai. He used to oversee work related to counting of donation money. He is accused of getting 8 months of CCTV footage deleted. Meanwhile, Anukalp Mishra also works at Ram Mandir. Team also suspects donations received by Sita Rasoi Trust On the other hand, the SIT investigation has also revealed the formation of a trust called Sita Rasoi. After investigating the donations taken in the name of this trust and their usage, it is being viewed with suspicion. It is believed that this trust will be in the crosshairs in the next phase of investigation. Received several hundred crores in donations at Mahakumbh, showed less During the Prayagraj Mahakumbh, crores of devotees also visited Ram Mandir. The temple trust set up camps and collected donations. The investigation team found less donation money during that period, which has raised suspicions. It is believed that several hundred crores of rupees were received in donations at that time, whereas not even half of it was shown. The team may further investigate how many more trusts have been created in the name of Ramlalla to collect donation money. They were warned not to leave Ayodhya SP chief and former minister had raised the issue of theft Pawan Pandey, who was a minister in the SP government, claimed on June 7 that between 5 to 7.5 crore rupees were stolen from the Ram Temple. Party chief Akhilesh also said that the government's silence on the matter is suspicious. The court should look into the matter. Champat Rai had clarified that no such matter has come to light so far. When the controversy escalated, BJP leader Dr. Rajnish Singh wrote a letter to the Prime Minister on June 9 demanding a CBI inquiry. The next day, on June 10, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) sought a report on the matter from the temple trust. Nripendra Mishra said - Ram Temple offerings were looted Nripendra Mishra, former IAS officer and Chairman of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple Construction Committee, said that the theft of offerings at Ram Temple was an open loot. The entire management of the temple should be changed. This is a huge betrayal of the people. The bank officials did not fulfill their responsibility. What could be greater negligence than this. These statements were made by Nripendra Mishra in a conversation with ABP News on Friday. He said - Evidence related to the counting process shows that surveillance in the entire system was almost zero and there was a serious lack of vigilance. Whereas, in the agreement between the bank and the trust, it was clearly stipulated that the responsibility of counting donations and maintaining their accounts would be the bank's. Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Mishra had also said, 'Champat Rai is the doer and bearer of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust. I will not question Champat Rai's dedication. He has been associated with the temple movement for the past 35 years. But there has been a lapse in supervision. Those who commit dishonesty in offerings will be cursed for 7 generations.' Yogi had said in Ayodhya - whoever the criminal is, will not be spared CM Yogi reached Ayodhya on Friday, June 19, amidst the controversy over theft of offerings at Ram Temple. He performed worship at Hanumangarhi Temple. After that, he reached Ram Temple and had darshan of Ram Lalla. Yogi said - Opposition people used to get bullets fired for chanting Ram's name. Look at their hypocritical character. Congress made every effort to ensure that Ram Temple could not be built. They shamelessly said in the Supreme Court that Ram never existed. The same Congress is now very agitated about Ayodhya. Yogi said in the public meeting - Look at the dual character of SP, they say that Ram devotees have been insulted. The people who ordered firing on Kar Sevaks and Ram devotees are now giving sermons. We have set up an SIT investigation at the request of the Trust. The SIT will separate milk from water. I would tell everyone not to make any irresponsible comments that hurt Ram devotees. Whom did the SIT interrogate in 6 days, know What did people say about the Ram Temple donation theft A CEO may also be appointed at Ram Temple Sources have claimed that a CEO (Chief Executive Officer) appointment similar to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple may be made at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The government may take this step to strengthen financial transparency and accountability. A senior IAS officer may be appointed as CEO to oversee the trust's administrative and financial functions. This appointment aims to make donations, accounts, and administrative arrangements more transparent. Deliberations are being held at the government and trust levels before making the final decision. Claim - 1250 Shri Ram bricks of gold and silver missing Dharmasena founder Santosh Dubey claims that 1250 bricks made of gold-silver, diamonds-rubies and ashtadhatu (eight metals) that came to Ayodhya in 1989 after being worshipped from village to village, city to city, and from within the country and abroad, have now 'disappeared'. These slabs remained in Karsevakpuram until 2002. The worshipped clay slabs are still kept in Karsevakpuram, but the metal slabs are nowhere to be seen. According to Santosh Dubey, the responsibility of looking after the gold and silver slabs was also with the Trust's General Secretary Champat Rai. stories.title: Ram Mandir theft row:Relatives of Trustees bought land at 17 times the cost, demanded 40% construction material commission
stories.summary: In a development likened by sources to the proverb ‘Andha baatein rewari, ghar gharana khaaye’, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Temple has reportedly uncovered the deep involvement of relatives and close associates of key temple functionaries in various aspects of temple operations. According to sources, the investigation has found that from the counting of offerings to broader administrative management, individuals linked to Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao had established a strong presence within the temple system. The SIT has also reportedly identified irregularities in land acquisitions and construction-related transactions. Allegations include the purchase of land at up to 17 times the circle rate and the payment of 40% commissions on construction materials. Sources indicate that the SIT may submit its preliminary report to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday. The findings have fuelled speculation that the Ram Temple Trust could be dissolved and reconstituted. Champat Rai's nephew under scrutiny over land purchases Chandan Rai, nephew of Temple Trust General Secretary Champat Rai, has emerged as a key figure in the land acquisition investigation. According to sources, Chandan was living in a rented house in the Ram Ghat area until last year. He has since reportedly acquired several bighas of land in Ayodhya's Majha region and built a hotel in Haridwar. The Temple Trust required 107 acres of land for expansion and, over five years, purchased plots located between 500 metres and 3 kilometres from Ram Janmabhoomi, allegedly paying around 17 times the circle rate. Several of these plots were reportedly Nazul (government-owned) land or registered in the names of temples, making their sale legally contentious. Sources allege that Chandan Rai played a significant role in these transactions. The SIT has seized all relevant land purchase documents for examination. Land deals raising questions 2021 February- 7,285 sq ft of land near the Ram Janmabhoomi complex purchased for ₹1 crore. 27 March- Land belonging to Fakire Ram Temple purchased for ₹4 crore. Since temple land cannot ordinarily be registered, the matter is currently before the courts. March 2 April 2024 A 6,450 sq metre residential plot in Kot Ramchander village was purchased from Murlidas for ₹23.61 crore. Its estimated value was ₹2.92 crore. The land is classified as Nazul land. 2025 May In Haibatpur village, 7,416 sq metres of residential land was purchased from Gurdeyi for ₹9.09 crore, despite an estimated value of ₹2.96 crore. Another 6,220 sq metres of non-agricultural land was purchased from Ram Adhar for ₹7.62 crore, with an estimated value of ₹2.48 crore. July 3,540 sq metres of land, located 500 metres from the temple, purchased from the Transport Corporation for ₹6.9 crore. August In Haibatpur, 5,480 sq metres of agricultural land purchased from Shivpujan for ₹6.7 crore, despite a valuation of ₹88.7 lakh. In Bagh Bijaisi, 4,080 sq metres of non-agricultural land purchased for ₹6.45 crore, although valued at ₹1.95 crore. The plot is located around one kilometre from the temple. November 7,780 sq metres of land on Lucknow Road purchased from Tanvi Bansal for ₹29.67 crore; circle-rate valuation was ₹1.73 crore. In the same month, 14,730 sq metres purchased from Alok Bansal for ₹55.47 crore against a circle-rate value of ₹9 crore. The land is situated around 3 kilometres from the temple and was used as temporary parking during the Pran Pratishtha ceremony. Gopal Rao's nephew allegedly held significant influence Somesh Anand, nephew of Gopal Rao, a special invitee responsible for temple arrangements, has also come under scrutiny. Both belong to Hubli, Karnataka. According to sources, Somesh allegedly transported materials to Karnataka by train and returned by air on numerous occasions, making more than 50 such trips over the past three to four years. The SIT reportedly found that contractors involved in temple construction could not receive payment without Somesh's approval. Payments for construction materials were also allegedly routed through him. Sources further claim that he had the authority to issue VVIP passes and could freely access the room where offerings were counted, despite his official responsibility being limited to wheelchair arrangements within the temple complex. ₹36 lakh recovered from Tinnu Yadav's nephew Manish, nephew of Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, was assigned duties in the room where offerings were counted. According to information received by the SIT, a raid on Tinnu's ancestral home in the Swargdwar locality led to the recovery of ₹36 lakh, allegedly based on information provided by Manish. Sources claim that Tinnu secured his nephew's placement in the offerings-counting unit and subsequently positioned a network of trusted associates there. It is alleged that members of the group diverted portions of the offerings and later shared the proceeds among themselves. Following questioning by the SIT on 13 June, Manish has reportedly been barred from leaving the temple premises. Relatives of Anil Mishra accused in offering theft case Anukalp Mishra and Lavkush Mishra, relatives of Trust member Dr Anil Mishra, have also come under investigation. Anukalp was reportedly assigned to the offerings-counting process on Dr Mishra's recommendation. Five months ago, he allegedly arranged employment for his brother-in-law, Lavkush Mishra, in the same unit. Following the emergence of the theft allegations, Trust members reportedly recovered ₹12 lakh hidden beneath a stack of cow-dung cakes at Lavkush Mishra's residence. Lavkush is also said to be constructing a house in Ayodhya, while Anukalp recently purchased a property worth ₹65 lakh in Kaushalpuri Colony. Ratnesh and Gagandeep under investigation Ratnesh Chaturvedi and Gagandeep Singh are not related to any Trust member, but sources describe both as close associates of Champat Rai. The pair were reportedly part of the team responsible for transporting offerings from the temple to the bank, having been appointed on Champat Rai's recommendation. According to sources, Ratnesh, Gagandeep and Tinnu would often leave together after depositing the offerings at the bank. Rather than returning directly to the temple, they allegedly travelled to a separate location where portions of the offerings were distributed. The SIT has questioned both men and currently considers them suspects in the investigation.
